verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE, glittering maids send Sura forth, the glorious sisters, close-allied, Send Indu forth, their mighty Lord.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pervade, O Pavamana, all our treasures with repeated light, God, coming hither from the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pour on us, Pavamana, rain, as service and rain praise for Gods: Pour all to be our nourishment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou art a Steer by lustre: we, O Pavamana, faithfully Call upon thee the Splendid One.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Do thou, rejoicing, nobly-armed! pour upon us heroic strength: O Indu, come thou bitherward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When thou art cleansed with both the hands and dipped in waters, with the wood. Thou comest to the gathering-place.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sing forth your songs, as Vyasva sang, to Soma Pavamana, to, The Mighty One with thousand eyes;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whose coloured sap they drive with stones, the yellow meath-distilling juice, Indu for Indra, for his drink.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We seek to gain the friendly love of thee that Strong and Mighty One, Of thee the winner of all wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Flow onward with thy stream, a Steer, inspiriting the Maruts' Lord, Winning all riches by thy might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I send thee forth to battle from the press, O Pavamana, Strong, Sustainer, looker on the light.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Acknowledged by this song of mine, flow, tawny-coloured, with thy stream Incite to battle thine ally.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indu, visible to all pour out for us abundant food: Soma, be thou our prosperer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The pitchers, Indu, with thy streams have sung aloud in vigorous might Enter them, and let Indra drink.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O thou whose potent gladdening juice they milk out with the stones, flow on, Destroyer of our enemies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: King Pavamana is implored with holy songs, on man's behalf, To travel through the firmament.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring us, O Indu, hundredfold increase of kine, and noble steeds, The gift of fortune for our help.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pressed for the banquet of the Gods, O Soma, bring us might, and speed, Like beauty for a brilliant show.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma, flow on exceeding bright with loud roar to the wooden vats, Falcon-like resting in thine home.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma, the Water-winner flows to Indra, Vayu, Varuna, To Visnu and the Marut host.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma , bestowing food upon our progeny, from every sides, Pour on us riches thousand fold
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Soma juices which have been expressed afar or near at hand, Or there on Saryanavan's bank,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Those pressed among Arjikas, pressed among the active, in men's homes, Or pressed among the Races Five-
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May these celestial drops, expressed, pour forth upon us, as they flow, Rain from the heavens apd hero strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Urged forward o'er the ox-hide flows the Lovely One of tawny hue, Lauded by Jamadagni's song.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like horses urged to speed, the drops, bright, stirring vital power, when blent With milk, are beautified in streams.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So they who toil with juices send thee forward for the Gods' repast: So with this splendour flow thou on.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We choose to-day that chariot-steed of thine, the Strong, that brings us bliss, The Guardian, the desire of all,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Excellent, the Gladdener, the Sage with heart that understands, The Guardian, the desire of all;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who for ourselves, O thou Most Wise, is wealth and fair intelligence, The Guardian, the desire of all.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FOR holy lore of every sort, flow onward thou whom all men love. A Friend to be besought by friends.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O'er all thou rulest with these Two which, Soma Pavamana, stand, Turned, as thy stations, hitherward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wise Soma Pavamana, thou encompassest on every side Thy stations as the seasons come.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Flow onward, generating food, for precious boons of every kind, A Friend for friends, to be our help.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Upon the lofty ridge of heaven thy bright rays with their essences, Soma, spread purifying power.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Soma, these Seven Rivers flow, as being thine, to give command: The Streams of milk run forth to thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Flow onward, Soma in a stream, effused to gladden Indra's heart, Bringing imperishable fame.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Driving thee in Vivasvan's course, the Seven Sisters with their hymns Made melody round thee the Sage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The virgins deck thee o'er fresh streams to drive thee to the sieve when thou, A singer, bathest in the wood.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The streams of Pavamana, thine, Sage, Mighty One, have pouredthem forth. Like coursers eager for renown.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They have been poured upon the fleece towards the meath-distilling vat: The holy songs have sounded forth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like milch-kine coming home, the drops of Soma juice have reached the lake, Have reached the place of sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indu, to our great delight the running waters flow to us, When thou wilt robe thyself in milk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In this thy friendship, and with thee to help us, fain to sacrifice, Indu, we crave thy friendly love.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Flow on, O Soma, for the great Viewer of men, for gain of Idne Enter thou into Indra's throat.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Best art thou, Soma, of the great, Strongest of strong ones, Indu: thou As Warrior ever hast prevailed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mightier even than the strong, more valiant even than the brave, More liberal than the bountiful,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma, as Sura, bring us food, win offspring of our bodies: we Elect thee for our friendship, we elect thee for companionship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, thou pourest life; send down upon us food and vigorous strength; Drive thou misfortune far away,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni is Pavamana, Sage, Chief Priest of all the Races Five: To him whose wealth is great we pray.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Skilled in thy task, O Agni, pour splendour with hero strength on us, Granting me wealth that nourishes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Beyond his enemies away to sweet praise Pavamana flows, Like Surya visible to all.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Adorned by living men, set forth for entertainment, rich in food, Far-sighted Indu is a Steed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, Pavamana, hath produced the lofty Law, the brilliant light, Destroying darkness black of hue.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From tawny Pavamana, the Destroyer, radiant streams have sprung, Quick streams from him whose gleams are swift.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Best rider of the chariot, praised with fairest praise mid beauteous ones, Gold-gleaming with the Marut host,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Pavamana, best to win the booty, penetrate with rays, Giving the singer hero strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Over the fleecy sieve hath flowed the drop effused: to Indra comes Indu while he is purified
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This Soma, through the pressing-stones, is sporting on the oxhide, and Summoning Indra to the draught.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Pavamana, bless us, so that we may live, with that bright milk Of thine which hath been brought from heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THOU, Soma, hast a running stream, joyous, most strong at sacrifice: Flow bounteously bestowing wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Effused as cheerer of the men, flowing best gladdener, thou art A Prince to Indra with thy juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Poured forth by pressing-stones, do thou with loud roar send us in a stream Most excellent illustrious might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indu, urged forward, floweth through the fleecy cloth: the Tawny One With his loud roar hath brought as strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indu, thou flowest through the fleece, bringing felicities and fame, And, Soma, spoil and wealth in kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hither, O Indu, bring us wealth in steeds and cattle hundredfold: Bring wealth, O Soma, thousand fold.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In purifying, through the sieve the rapid drops of'Soma juice Come nigh to Indra in their course.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For Indra floweth excellent Indu, the noblest Soma juice The Living for the Living One.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The glittering maids send Sura forth they with their song have sung aloud To Pavamana dropping meath.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Pusan, drawn by goats, be our protector, and on all his paths Bestow on us our share of maids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This Soma flows like gladdening oil for him who wears the braided locks: He shall give us our share of maids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This Soma juice, O glowing God, flows like pure oil, effused for thee: He shall give us our share of maids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Flow onward, Soma, in thy stream, begetter of the sages' speech: Wealth-giver among Gods art thou.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Falcon dips within the jars: he wrap him in his robe and goes Loud roaring to the vats of wood.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma, thy juice hath been effused and poured into the pitcher: like A rapid hawk it rushes on.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For Indra flow most rich in sweets, O Soma, bringing him delight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They were sent forth to feast the Gods, like chariots that display their strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Brilliant, best givers of delight, these juices have sent Vayu forth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bruised by the press-stones and extolled, Soma, thou goest to the sieve, Giving the worshipper hero strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This juice bruised by the pressing-stones and lauded passes through the sieve, Slayer of demons, through the fleece.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Pavamana, drive away the danger, whether near at hand Or far remote, that finds me here.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This day may Pavamana cleanse us with his purifying power, Most active purifying Priest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, with the cleansing light diffused through all thy fiery glow, Purify thou this prayer of ours.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Cleanse us with thine own cleansing power, O Agni, that is bright with flame, And by libations poured to thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Savitar, God, by both of these, libation, purifying power, Purify me on every side.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Cleanse us, God Savitar, with Three, O Soma, with sublimest forms, Agni, with forms of power and might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the Gods' company make me clean, and Vasus make rue pure by song. Purify me, ye General Gods; O Jatavedas, make me pure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fill thyself full of juice, flow forth, O Soma, thou with all thy stalks, The best oblation to the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We with our homage have approached the Friend who seeks our wondering praise, Young, strengthener of the solemn rite.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lost is Alayya's axe. O Soma, God do thou send it back hither in thy flow Even, Soma, God, if 'twere a mole.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The man who reads the essence stored by saints, the Pavamani hymns, Tastes food completely purified, made sweet by Matarisvan's touch.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoever reads the essence stored by saints, the Pavamani hymns, Sarasvati draws forth for him water and butter, milk and meath.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE drops of Soma juice like cows who yield their milk have flowed forth, rich in meath, unto the Shining One, And, seated on the grass, raising their voice, assumed the milk, the covering robe wherewith the udders stream.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He bellows with a roar around the highest twigs: the Tawny One is sweetened as he breaks them up. Then passing through the sieve into the ample room, the God throws off the dregs according to his wish.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The gladdening drink that measured out the meeting Twins fills full with milk the Eternal Ever-waxing Pair. Bringing to light the Two great Regions limitless, moving above them he gained sheen that never fades.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wandering through, the Parents, strengthening the floods, the Sage makes his place swell with his own native might. The stalk is mixed with grain: he comes led by the men together with the sisters, and preserves the Head.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With energetic intellect the Sage is born, deposited as germ of Law, far from the Twins. They being young at first showed visibly distinct the Creature that is half-concealed and half-exposed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The sages knew the form of him the Gladdener, what time the Falcon brought the plant from far away. Him who assures success they beautified in streams, the stalk who yearned therefor, mighty and meet for praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Together with the Rsis, with their prayers and hymns ten women deck thee, Soma, friendly when effused. Led by the men, with invocations of the Gods, through the fleece, thou hast given us strength to win the spoil.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Songs resonant with praise have celebrated him. Soma, Friend, springing forth with his fair company. Even him who rich in meath, with undulating stream, Winnner of Wealth, Immortal, sends his voice from heaven,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He sends it into all the region forth from heaven. Soma, while he is filtered, settles in the jars. With milk and waters is he decked when pressed with stones: Indu, when purified, shall find sweet rest and room.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even thus poured forth How on thy way, O Soma, vouchsafing us most manifold lively vigour. We will invoke benevolent Earth and Heaven. Give us, ye Gods, riches with noble heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LAID like an arrow on the bow the hymn hath been loosed like a young calf to the udder of its dam. As one who cometh first with full stream she is milked the Soma is impelled to this man's holy rites.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The thought is deeply fixed; the savoury juice is shed; the tongue with joyous sound is stirring in the mouth; And Pavamana, like the shout of combatants, the drop rising in sweet juice, is flowing through the fleece.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He flows about the sheep-skin, longing for a bride: he looses Aditi's Daughters for the worshipper. The sacred drink hath come, gold-tinted, well-restrained: like a strong Bull he shines, whetting his manly might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Bull is bellowing; the Cows are coming nigh: the Goddesses approach the God's own resting-place. Onward hath Soma passed through the sheep's fair bright fleece, and hath, as 'twere, endued a garment newly washed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The golden-hued, Immortal, newly bathed, puts on a brightly shining vesture that is never harmed. He made the ridge of heaven to be his radiant robe, by sprinkling of the bowls from moisture of the sky.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even as the beams of Surya, urging men to speed, that cheer and send to sleep, together rush they forth, These swift outpourings in long course of holy rites: no form save only Indra shows itself so pure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As down the steep slope of a river to the vale, drawn from the Steer the swift strong draughts have found a way. Well be it with the men and cattle in our home. May powers, O Soma, may the people stay with us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pour out upon us wealth in goods, in gold, in steeds, in cattle and in corn, and great heroic strength. Ye, Soma, are my Fathers, lifted up on high as heads of heaven and makers of the strength of life.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These Pavamanas here, these drops of Soma, to Indra have sped forth like cars to booty. Effused, they pass the cleansing fleece, while, gold-hued, they cast their covering off to pour the rain down.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indu, flow thou on for lofty Indra, flow blameless, very gracious, foe-destroyer. Bring splendid treasures to the man who lauds thee. O Heaven and Earth, with all the Gods protect us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE three times seven Milch-kine in the eastern heaven have for this Soma poured the genuine milky draught. Four other beauteous Creatures hath he made for his adornment, when he waxed in strength through holy rites.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Longing for lovely Amrta, by his wisdom he divided, each apart from other, earth and heaven. He gladly wrapped himself in the most lucid floods, when through their glory they found the God's resting-place.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May those his brilliant rays he ever free from death, inviolate, for both classes of created things,- Rays wherewith powers of men and Gods are purified. Yea, even for this have sages welcomed him as King.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, while he is adorned by the ten skillful ones, that he too in the Midmost Mothers may create, While he is watching o'er the lovely Amrta's ways, looks on both races as Beholder of mankind.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, while he is adorned to stream forth mighty strength, rejoices in his place between the earth and heaven. The Steer dispels the evil-hearted with his might, aiming at offerings as an archer at the game.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Beholding, as it were, Two Mother Cows, the Steer goes roaring on his way even as the Maruts roar. Knowing Eternal Law, the earliest light of heaven, he, passing wise, was chosen out to tell it forth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The fearful Bull is bellowing with violent might, far-sighted, sharpening his yellow coloured horns. Soma assumes his seat in the well-fashioned place: the cowhide and the sheepskin are his ornament.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bright, making pure his body free from spot and stain, on the sheep's back the Golden-coloured hath flowed down. Acceptable to Mitra, Vayu, Varuna, he is prepared as threefold meal by skillful men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Flow on for the God's banquet, Soma, as a Steer, and enter Indra's heart, the Soma's reservoir. Bear us beyond misfortune ere we be oppressed. the man who knows the land directs the man who asks.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Urged like a car-steed flow to strength, O Soma: Indu, flow onward to the throat of Indra. Skilled, bear us past, as in a boat o'er water: as battling Hero save us from the foeman.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE guerdon is bestowed: the Mighty takes his Seat, and, ever-Watchful, guards from fiend and evil sprite. Gold-hued, he makes the cloud his diadem, the milk his carpet in both worlds, and prayer his robe of state.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong, bellowing, he goes, like one who slays the folk; he lets this hue of Asuras flow off from him, Throws off his covering, seeks his father's meeting-place, and thus makes for himself the bright robe he assumes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Onward he flows, from both the hands, pressed out with stones: excited by the prayer, the water makes him wild. He frolics and draws near, completes his work with song, and bathes in streams to satisfy the worshipper.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They pour out meath around the Master of the house, Celestial Strengthener of the mountain that gives might; In whom, through his great powers, oblation-eating cows in their uplifted udder mix their choicest milk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They, the ten sisters, on the lap of Aditi, have sent him forward like a car from both the arms. He wanders and comes near the Cow's mysterious place, even the place which his inventions have produced.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like as a falcon to his home, so speeds the God to his own golden wisely-fashioned place to rest. With song they urge the darling to the sacred grass: the Holy One goes like a courser to the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From far away, from heaven, the red hued noted Sage, Steer of the triple height, hath sung unto the kine. With thousand guidings he, leading this way and that, shines, as a singer, splendidly through many a morn.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His covering assumes a radiant hue; where'er he comes into the fight he drives the foe afar. The Winner of the Floods, with food he seeks the host of heaven, he comes to praises glorified with milk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like a bull roaming round the herds he bellows: he hath assumed the brilliancy of Surya. Down to the earth hath looked the heavenly Falcon: Soma with wisdom views all living creatures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THEY cleanse the Gold-hued: like a red Steed is he yoked, and Soma in the jar is mingled with the milk. He sendeth out his voice, and many loving friends of him the highly lauded hasten with their songs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The many sages utter words in unison, while into Indra's throat they pour the Soma juice, When, with the ten that dwell together closely joined, the men whose hands are skillful cleanse the lovely meath.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He goes upon his way, unresting, to the cows, over the roaring sound which Sarya's Daughter loves. The Falcon brought it to him for his own delight: now with the twofold kindred sisters is his home.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Washed by the men, stone-pressed, dear on the holy grass, faithful to seasons, Lord of cattle from of old, Most liberal, completing sacrifice for men, O Indra, pure bright Soma, Indu, flows for thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra, urged by arms of men and poured in streams, Soma flows on for thee after his Godlike kind. Plans thou fulfillest, gatherest thoughts for sacrifice: in the bowls sits the Gold-hued like a roosting bird.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sages well-skilled in work, intelligent, drain out the stalk that roars, the Sage, the Everlasting One. The milk, the hymns unite them with him in the place of sacrifice, his seat who is produced anew.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Earth's central point, sustainer of the mighty heavens, distilled into the streams, into the waters' wave, As Indra's thunderbolt, Steer with far spreading wealth, Soma is flowing on to make the heart rejoice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Over the earthly region flow thou on thy way, helping the praiser and the pourer, thou Most Wise. Let us not lack rich treasure reaching to our home, and may we clothe ourselves in manifold bright wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hither, O Indu, unto us a hundred gifts of steeds, a thousand gifts of cattle and of gold, Measure thou forth, yea, splendid ample strengthening food do thou, O Pavamana, heed this laud of ours.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THEY from the spouting drop have sounded at the rim: naves speed together to the place of sacrifice. That Asura hath formed, to seize, three lofty heights. The ships of truth have borne the pious man across.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The strong Steers, gathering, have duly stirred themselves, and over the stream's wave the friends sent forth the song. Engendering the hymn, with flowing streams of meath, Indra's dear body have they caused to wax in strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With sanctifying gear they sit around the song: their ancient Father guards their holy work from harm. Varuna hath o'erspread the mighty sea of air. Sages had power to hold him in sustaining floods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sweet-tongued, exhaustless, they have sent their voices down together, in heaven's vault that pours a thousand streams. His wildly-restless warders never close an eye: in every place are found the bonds that bind man last.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O'er Sire and Mother they have roared in unison bright with the verse of praise, burning up riteless men, Blowing away with supernatural might from earth and from the heavens the swarthy skin which Indra hates.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Those which, as guides of song and counsellors of speed, were manifested from their ancient dwelling place,- From these the eyeless and the deaf have turned aside: the wicked travel not the pathway of the Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time the filter with a thousand streams is stretched, the thoughtful sages purify their song therein. Bright-coloured are their spies, vigorous, void of guile, excellent, fair to see, beholders of mankind.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Guardian of Law, most wise, he may not be deceived: three Purifiers hath he set within his heart. With wisdom he beholds all creatures that exist: he drives into the pit the hated riteless ones.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The thread of sacrifice spun in the cleansing sieve, on Varuna's tongue-tip, by supernatural might,- This, by their striving, have the prudent ones attained: he who hath not this power shall sink into the pit.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: BORN like a youngling he hath clamoured in the wood, when he, the Red, the Strong, would win the light of heaven. He comes with heavenly seed that makes the water swell: him for wide-spreading shelter we implore with prayer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A far-extended pillar that supports the sky the Soma-stalk, filled full, moves itself every way. He shall bring both these great worlds while the rite proceeds: the Sage holds these who move! together and all food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wide space hath he who follows Aditi's right path, and mighty, well-made food, meath blent with Soma juice; He who from hence commands the rain, Steer of the kine, Leader of floods, who helps us hence, who claims our laud.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Butter and milk are drawn from animated cloud; thence Amrta is produced, centre of sacrifice. Him the Most Bounteous Ones, ever united, love; him as our Friend the Men who make all swell rain down.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Soma-stalk hath roared, following with the wave: he swells with sap for man the skin which Gods enjoy. Upon the lap of Aditi he lays the germ, by means whereof we gain children and progeny.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In the third region which distils a thousand streams, may the Exhaustless Ones descend with procreant power. The kindred Four have been sent downward from the heavens: dropping with oil they bring Amrta and sacred gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma assumes white colour when he strives to gain: the bounteous Asura knows full many a precious boon. Down the steep slope, through song, he comes to sacrifice, and he will burst the water-holding cask of heaven,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, to the shining milk-anointed beaker, as to his goal, hath stepped the conquering Courser. Pious-souled men have sent their gift of cattle unto Kaksivan of the hundred winters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma, thy juice when thou art blended with the streams, flows, Pavamana, through the long wool of the sheep. So, cleansed by sages. O best giver of delight, grow sweet for Indra, Pavamana! for his drink.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GRACIOUSLY-MINDED he is flowing on his way to win dear names o'er which the Youthful One grows great. The Mighty and Far-seeing One hath mounted now the mighty Surya's car which moves to every side.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Speaker, unassailable Master of this hymn, the Tongue of sacrifice pours forth the pleasant meath. Within the lustrous region of the heavens the Son makes the third secret name of Mother and of Sire.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sending forth flashes he hath bellowed to the jars, led by the men into the golden reservoir. The milky streams of sacrifice have sung to him: he of the triple height shines brightly through the morns.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pressed by the stones, with hymns, and graciously inclined, illuminating both the Parents, Heaven and Earth, He flows in ordered season onward through the flee, a current of sweet juice still swelling day by day.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Flow onward, Soma, flow to bring prosperity: cleansed by the men, invest thee with the milky draught. What gladdening drinks thou hast, foaming, exceeding strong, even with these incite Indra to give us wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: ON flows the potent juice, sustainer of the heavens, the strength of Gods, whom men must hail with shouts of joy. The Gold-hued, started like a courser by brave men, impetuously winneth splendour in the streams.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He takes his weapons, like a hero, in his hands, fain to win light, car-borne, in forays for the kine. Indu, while stimulating India's might, is urged forward and balmed by sages skillful in their task.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma, as thou art purified with flowing wave, exhibiting thy strength enter thou Indra's throat. Make both worlds stream for us, as lightning doth the clouds: mete out exhaustless powers for us, as 'twere through song.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Onward he flows, the King of all that sees the light: the Rsis' Lord hath raised the song of sacrifice; Even he who is adorned with Surya's arrowy beam, Father of hymns, whose wisdom is beyond our reach.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like as a bull to herds, thou flowest to the pail, bellowing as a steer upon the water's lap. So, best of Cheerers, thou for Indra flowest on that we, with thy protection, may o'ercome in fight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MORE beauteous than the beautiful, as Indra's bolt, this Soma, rich in sweets, hath clamoured in the vat. Dropping with oil, abundant, streams of sacrifice flow unto him like milch-kine, lowing, with their milk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: On flows that Ancient One whom, hitherward, from heaven, sped through the region of the air, the Falcon snatched. He, quivering with alarm and terrified in heart before bow-armed Krsanu, holdeth fast the sweet.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May those first freshest drops of Soma juice effused flow on, their way to bring us mighty strength in kine. Beauteous as serpents, worthy to be looked upon, they whom each sacred gift and all our prayers have pleased.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May that much-lauded Indu, with a heart inclined to us, well-knowing, fight against our enemies. He who hath brought the germ beside the Strong One's seat moves onward to the widely-opened stall of kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The active potent juice of heaven is flowing on, great Varuna whom the forward man can ne'er deceive. Mitra, the Holy, hath been pressed for troubled times, neighing like an impatient horse amid the herd.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: RAISING his voice the King hath flowed upon his way: invested with the waters he would win the kine. The fleece retains his solid parts as though impure, and bright and cleansed he seeks the special place of Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Soma, art effused for Indra by the men, balmed in the wood as wave, Sage, Viewer of mankind. Full many are the paths whereon thou mayest go: a thousand bay steeds hast thou resting in the bowls.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Apsarases who dwell in waters of the sea, sitting within, have flowed to Soma wise of heart. They urge the Master of the house upon his way, and to the Eternal Pavamana pray for bliss.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma flows on for u's as winner of the kine, winner of thousands, cars, water, and light, and gold; He whom the Gods have made a gladdening draught to drink, the drop most sweet to taste, weal-bringing, red of hue.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma, as Pavamana thou, our faithful Friend, making for us these real treasures, flowest on. Slay thou the enemy both near and far away: grant us security and ample pasturage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SPONTANEOUS let our drops of Soma juice flow on, pressed, golden-hued, among the Gods of lofty heaven. Perish among us they who give no gifts of food! perish the godless! May our prayers obtain success.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Forward to us the drops, distilling meath, shall flow, like riches for whose sake we urge the horses on. Beyond the crafty hindering of all mortal men may we continually bear precious wealth away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, verily, foe of hate shown to himself is he, yea, verity, destroyer too of other hate. As thirst subdueth in the desert, conquer thou, O Soma Pavarnana, men of evil thoughts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Near kin to thee is he, raised loftiest in the heavens: upon the earth's high ridge thy scions have grown forth. The press-stones chew and crunch thee on the ox's hide: sages have milked thee with their hands into the streams.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So do they hurry on thy strong and beauteous juice, O Indu, as the first ingredient of the draught. Bring low, thou Pavamana, every single foe, and be thy might shown forth as sweet and gladdening drink.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: ON flows the stream of Soma who beholds mankind: by everlasting Law he calls the Gods from heaven. He lightens with the roaring of Br aspati: h the lakes have not contained the pourings of juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, powerful Soma, thou to whom the cows have -lowed, ascendest bright with sheen, thine iron-fashioned home. Thou, lengthening our princes' life and high renown, flowest for Indra as his might to gladdening drink.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Best giver of delight, he flows to Indra's throat, robing himself in might, Auspicious One, for fame. He spreads himself abroad to meet all things that be: the vigorous Tawny Steed flows sporting on his way.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The men, the ten swift fingers, milk thee out for Gods, even thee most rich in meath, with thousand flowing streams. Soma who winnest thousands, driven by the men, expressed with stones, bring, as thou flowest, all the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Deft-handed men with stones, the ten swift fingers, drain thee into waters, thee, the Steer enriched with sweets. Thou, Soma, gladdening Indra, and the Heavenly Host, flowest as Pavamana like a river's wave.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: ONWARD to Indra's throat move, beauteously adorned, the waves of Soma as he purifies himself, When they, brought forward with the lovely curd of kine, effused, have cheered the Hero to bestow his gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hither hath Soma flowed unto the beakers, like a chariot-horse, a stallion swift upon his way. Thus, knowing both the generations, he obtains the rights and dues of Gods from yonder and from hence.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: While thou art cleansed, O Soma, scatter wealth on us; Indu, bestow great bounty as a liberal Prince. Giver of life, with wisdom help to opulence; strew not our home possessions far away from us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hither let Pusan Pavamana come to us, Varuna, Mitra, bountiful, of one accord, The Maruts, Asvins, Vayu, and Brhaspati, Savitar, Tvastar, tractable Sarasvati.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Both Heaven and Earth, the all-invigorating Pair, Vidhatar, Aditi, and Aryaman the God, Bhaga who blesses men, the spacious Firmament,-let all the Gods in Pavamana take delight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: EVEN as a King hath Soma, red and tawny Bull, been pressed: the Wondrous One hath bellowed to the kine. While purified he passes through the filtering fleece to seat him hawk-like on the place that drops with oil.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To glory goest thou, Sage with disposing skill, like a groomed steed thou rushest forward to the prize. O Soma, be thou gracious, driving off distress: thou goest, clothed in butter, to a robe of state.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Parjanya is the Father of the Mighty Bird: on mountains, in earth's centre hath he made his home. The waters too have flowed, the Sisters, to the kine: he meets the pressing-stones at the beloved rite.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou givest pleasure as a wife delights her lord. Listen, O Child of Pajri, for to thee I speak. Amid the holy songs go on that we may live: in time of trouble, Soma, watch thou free from blame.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As to the men of old thou camest, Indu unharmed, to strengthen, winning hundreds, thousands, So now for new felicity flow onward: the waters follow as thy law ordaineth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SPREAD is thy cleansing filter, Brahmanaspati: as Prince, thou enterest its limbs from every side. The raw, whose mass hath not been heated gains not this: they only which are dressed, which bear, attain to it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: High in the seat of heaven is spread the Scorcher's sieve: its threads are standing separate, glittering with light. The Swift Ones favour him who purifieth this: with consciousness they stand upon the height of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The foremost spotted Steer hath made the Mornings shine, and yearning after strength sustains all things that be. By his high wisdom have the mighty Sages wrought: the Fathers who behold mankind laid down the germ,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Gandharva verily protects his dwelling place; Wondrous, he guards the generations of the Gods. Lord of the snare, he takes the foeman with the snare: those who are most devout have gained a share of meath.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rich in oblations! robed in cloud, thou compassest oblation, sacrifice, the mighty seat of Gods. King, on thy chariot-sieve thou goest up to war, and with a thousand weapons winnest lofty fame.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FLOW, cheering Gods, most active, winner of the flood, for Indra, and for Vayu, and for Varuna. Bestow on us to-day wide room with happiness, and in thine ample dwelling laud the Host of Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who hath come anear to creatures that have life, Immortal Soma flows onward to all of them. Effecting, for our aid, both union and release, Indu, like Surya, follows closely after Dawn.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who is poured with milk, he who within the plants hastes bringing treasure for the happiness of Gods, He, poured forth in a stream flows with the lightning's flash, Soma who gladdens Indra and the Host of Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Winner of thousands, he, this Soma, flows along, raising a vigorous voice that wakens with the dawn. Indu with winds drives on the ocean of the air, he sinks within the jars, he rests in Indra's heart.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The kine with milk dress him who makes the milk increase, Soma, amid the songs, who finds the light of heaven. Winner of wealth, the effectual juice is flowing on, Singer and Sage by wisdom, dear as heaven itself.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FLOW on to Indra, Soma, carefully effused: let sickness stay afar together with the fiends. Let not the double-tongued delight them with thy juice. here be thy flowing drops laden with opulence.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Pavamana, urge us forward in the fight thou art the vigour of the Gods, the well-loved drink. Smite thou our enemies who raise the shout of joy: Indra, drink Soma juice, and drive away our foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Unharmed, best Cheerer, thou, O Indu, flowest on: thou, even thou thyself, art Indra's noblest food. Full many a wise man lifts to thee the song of praise, and hails thee with a kiss as Sovran of this world.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wondrous, with hundred streams, hymned in a thousand songs, Indu pours out for Indra his delightful meath. Winning us land and waters, flow thou hitherward: Rainer of bounties, Soma, make broad way for us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Roaring within the beaker thou art balmed with milk: thou passest through the fleecy filter all at once. Carefully cleansed and decked like a prizewinning steed, O Soma, thou hast flowed down within Indra's throat.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Flow onward sweet of flavour for the Heavenly Race, for Indra sweet, whose name is easily invoked: Flow sweet for Mitra, Varuna, and Vayu, rich in meath, inviolable for Brhaspati.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ten rapid fingers deck the Courser in the jar: with hymns the holy singers send their voices forth. The filtering juices hasten to their eulogy, the drops that gladden find their way to Indra's heart.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: While thou art purified pour on us hero strength, great, far-extended shelter, spacious pasturage. Let no oppression master this our holy work: may we, O Indu, gain all opulence through thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Steer who sees afar hath risen above the sky: the Sage hath caused the lights of heaven to give their shine. The. King is passing through the filter with a roar: they drain the milk of heaven from him who looks on men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: High in the vault of heaven, unceasing, honey-tongued, the Loving Ones drain out the mountain-haunting Steer,- The drop that hath grown great in waters, in the lake meath-rich, in the stream's wave and in the cleansing sieve.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Loving Ones besought with many voices the Eagle who had flown away to heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: High to heaven's vault hath the Gandharva risen, beholding all his varied forms and figures. His ray hath shone abroad with gleaming splendour: pure, he hath lighted both the worlds, the Parents.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THY gladdening draughts, O Pavamana, urged by song flow swiftly of themselves like sons of fleet-foot mares. The drops of Soma juice, those eagles of the heavens, most cheering, rich in meath, rest in the reservoir.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As rapid chariot-steeds, so turned in several ways have thine exhilarating juices darted forth, Soma-drops rich in meath, waves, to the Thunder-armed, to Indra, like milch-kine who seek their calf with milk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like a steed urged to battle, finder of the light; speed onward to the cloud-born reservoir of heaven, A Steer that o'er the woolly surface seeks the sieve, Soma while purified for Indra's nourishment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fleet as swift steeds, thy drops, divine, thought-swift, have been, O Pavamana, poured with milk into the vat. The Rsis have poured in continuous Soma drops, ordainers who adorn thee, Friend whom Rsis love.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O thou who seest all things, Sovran as thou art and passing strong, thy rays encompass all abodes. Pervading with thy natural powers thou flowest on, and as the whole world's Lord, O Soma, thou art King.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The beams of Pavamana, sent from earth and heaven, his ensigns who is ever steadfast, travel round. When on the sieve the Golden-hued is cleansed, he rests within the vats as one who seats him in his place.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Served with fair rites he flows, ensign of sacrifice: Soma advances to the special place of Gods. He speeds with thousand currents to the reservoir, and passes through the filter bellowing as a bull.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Sovran dips him in the sea in and the streams, and set in rivers with the waters' wave moves on. High heaven's Sustainer at the central point of earth, raised on the fleecy surface Pavamana stands.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He on whose high decree the heavens and earth depend hath roared and thundered like the summit of the sky. Soma flows on obtaining Indra's friendly love, and, as they purify him, settles in the jars.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, light of sacrifice distils delicious meath, most wealthy, Father and begetter of the Gods. He, gladdening, best of Cheerers, juice hat Indra loves, enriches with mysterious treasure earth and heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The vigorous and far-seeing one, the Lord of heaven, flows, shouting to the beaker, with his thousand streams. Coloured like gold he rests in seats where Mitra dwells, the Steer made beautiful by rivers and by sheep.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In forefront of the rivers Pavamana speeds, in forefront of the hymn, foremost among the kine. He shares the mighty booty in the van of war: the well-armed Steer is purified by worshippers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This heedful Pavamana, like a bird sent forth, hath with his wave flowed onward to the fleecy sieve. O Indra, through thy wisdom, b thy thought, O Sage, Soma flows bright and pure between the earth and heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, clad in mail that reaches heaven, the Holy One, filling the firmament stationed amid the worlds, Knowing. the realm of light, hath come to us in rain: he summons to himself his own primeval Sire.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who was first of all to penetrate his form bestowed upon his race wide shelter and defense. From that high station which he hath in loftiest heaven he comes victorious to all encounters here.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indu hath started for Indra's special place and slights not as a Friend the promise of his Friend. Soma speeds onward like a youth to youthful maids, and gains the beaker by a course of hundred paths.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Your songs, exhilarating, tuneful, uttering praise, are come into the plains where the people meet. Worshippers have exalted Soma with their hymns, and milch kine have come near to meet him with their milk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Soma, Indu, while they cleanse thee, pour on us accumulateds Plentiful, nutritious food, Which, ceaseless, thrice a day shall yield us hero power enriched with store of nourishment, and strength, and Meath.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Far-seeing Soma flows, the Steer, the Lord of hymns, the Furtherer of day, of morning, and of heaven. Mixt with the streams he caused the beakers to resound, and with the singers' aid they entered Indra's heart.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: On, with the prudent singers, flows the ancient Sage and guided by the men hath roared about the vats. Producing Trita's name, may he pour forth the meath, that Vayu and that Indra may become his Friends.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, being purified, hath made the Mornings shine: this, even this is he who gave the rivers room. He made the Three Times Seven pour out the milky flow: Soma, the Cheerer, yields whate'er the heart finds sweet.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Flow, onward, Soma, in thine own celestial forms, flow, Indu, poured within the beaker and the sieve. Sinking into the throat of Indra with a roar, led by the men thou madest Surya mount to heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pressed out with stones thou flowest onward to the sieve, O Indu, entering the depths of Indra's throat. Far-sighted Soma, now thou lookest on mankind: thou didst unbar the cowstall for the Angirases.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In thee, O Soma, while thou purifitedst thee, high-thoughted sages, seeking favour, have rejoiced. Down from the heavens the Falcon brought thee hitherward, even thee, O Indu, thee whom all our hymns adorn.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Seven Milch-kine glorify the Tawny-coloured One while with his wave in wool he purifies himself. The living men, the mighty, have impelled the Sage into the waters' lap, the place of sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indu, attaining purity, plunges through the foe, making his ways all easy for the pious man. Making the kine his mantle, he, the lovely Sage, runs like a sporting courser onward through the fleece.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The ceaseless watery fountains with their hundred streams sing, as they hasten near, to him the Golden-hued Him, clad in robes of milk, swift fingers beautify on the third height and in the luminous realm of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These are thy generations of celestial seed thou art the Sovran Lord of all the world of life. This universe, O Pavamana, owns thy sway; thou, Indu, art the first establisher of Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou art the sea, O Sage who bringest all to light: under thy Law are these five regions of the world. Tlou reachest out beyond the earth, beyond the heavens: thine are the lights, O Pavamana, thine the Sun.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou in the filter, Soma Pavamana, art purified to support the region for the Gods. The chief, the longing ones have sought to hold thee fast, and all these living creatures have been turned to thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Onward the Singer travels o'er the fleecy sieve. the Tawny Steer hath bellowed in the wooden vats.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He hath assumed the rays of Surya for his robe, spinning, as he knows bow, the triply-twisted thread. He, guiding to the newest rules of Holy Law, comes as the Women's Consort to the special place.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: On flows the King of rivers and the Lord of heaven: he follows with a shout the paths of Holy Law. The Golden-hued is poured forth, with his hundred streams, Wealth-bringer, lifting up his voice while purified.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fain to be cleansed, thou, Pavamana, pourest out, like wondrous Surya, through the fleece, an ample sea. Purified with the hands, pressed by the men with stones, thou speedest on to mighty booty-bringing war.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Pavamana, sendest food and power in streams. thou sittest in the beakers as a hawk on trees, For Indra poured as cheering juice to make him glad, as nearest and farseeing bearer-up of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Sisters Seven, the Mothers, stand around the Babe, the noble, new-born Infant, skilled in holy song, Gandharva of the floods, divine, beholding men, Soma, that he may reign as King of all the world.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As Sovran Lord thereof thou Passest through these worlds, O Indu, harnessing thy tawny well-winged Mares. May they pour forth for thee milk and oil rich in sweets: O Soma, let the folk abide in thy decree.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Soma, thou beholdest men from every side: O Pavamana, Steer, thou wanderest through these. Pour out upon us wealth in treasure and in gold: may we have strength to live among the things that be.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Winner of gold and goods and cattle flow thou on, set as impregner, Indu, mid the worlds of life. Rich in brave men art thou, Soma, who winnest all: these holy singers wait upon thee with the song.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The wave of flowing meath hath wakened up desires: the Steer enrobed in milk plunges into the streams. Borne on his chariot-sieve the King hath risen to war, and with a thousand rays hath won him high renown.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dear to all life, he sends triumphant praises forth, abundant, bringing offspring, each succeeding day. From Indra crave for us, Indu, when thou art quaffed, the blessing that gives children, wealth that harbours steeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When days begin, the strong juice, lovely, golden-hued, is recognized by wisdom more and more each day, He, stirring both the Races, goes between the two, the bearer of the word of men and word of Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They balm him, balm him over balm him thoroughly, caress the mighty strength and balm it with the meath. They seize the flying Steer at the stream's breathing-place: cleansing with gold they grasp the Animal herein.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sing forth to Pavamana skilled in holy song: the juice is flowing onward like a mighty stream. He glideth like a serpent from his ancient skin, and like a playful horse the Tawny Steer hath run.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dweller in floods, King, foremost, he displays his might, set among living things as measurer of days. Distilling oil he flows, fair, billowy, golden-hued, borne on a car of light, sharing one home with wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Loosed is the heavens! support, the uplifted cheering juice: the triply-mingled draught flows round into the worlds. The holy hymns caress the stalk that claims our praise, when singers have approached his beauteous robe with song.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy streams that flow forth rapidly collected run over the fine fleece of the sheep as thou art cleansed. When, Indu, thou art balmed with milk within the bowl, thou sinkest in the jars, O Soma, when expressed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Winner of' power, flow, Soma, worthy of our laud: run onward to the fleece as well-beloved meath. Destroy, O Indu, all voracious Raksasas. With brave sons in the assembly let our speech be bold.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: RUN onward to the reservoir and seat thee: cleansed by the men speed forward to the battle. Making thee beauteous like an able courser, forth to the sacred grass with reins they lead thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indu, the well-armed God, is flowing onward, who quells the curse and guards from treacherous onslaught, Father, begetter of the Gods, most skillful, the buttress of the heavens and earth's supporter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rsi and Sage, the Champion of the people, cleft and sagacious, Usana in wisdom, He hath discovered even their hidden nature, the Cows' concealed and most mysterious title.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This thine own Soma rich in meath, O Indra, Steer for the Steer, hath flowed into the filter. The strong Free-giver, winning hundreds, thousands, hath reached the holy grass that never fails him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These Somas are for wealth of countless cattle, renown therefor, and mighty strength immortal. These have been sent forth, purified by strainers, like steeds who rush to battle fain for glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, while he cleanses him, invoked of many, hath flowed to give the people all enjoyment. Thou whom the Falcon brought, bring, dainty viands, bestir thyself and send us wealth and booty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This Soma, pressed into the cleansing filter, hath run as 'twere a host let loose, the Courser; Like a strong bull who whets his horns pen-pointed, like a brave warrior in the fray for cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He issued forth from out the loftiest mountain, and found kine hidden somewhere in a stable. Soma's stream clears itself for thee, O Indra, like lightning thundering through the clouds of heaven,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Cleansing thyself, and borne along with Indra, Soma, thou goest round the herd of cattle. May thy praise help us, Mighty One, prompt Giver, to the full ample food which thou bestowest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FOR thee this Soma is effused, O Indra: drink of this juice; for thee the stream is flowing- Soma, which thou thyself hast made and chosen, even Indu, for thy special drink to cheer thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like a capacious car hath it been harnessed, the Mighty; to acquire abundant treasures. Then in the sacrifice they celebrated all triumphs won by Nahusa in the battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like Vayu with his team, moving at pleasure, most gracious when invoked like both Nasatyas, Thou art thyself like the Wealth-Giver, Soma! who grants all boons, like song-inspiring Pusan.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like Indra who hath done great deeds, thou, Soma, art slayer of the Vrtras, Fort-destroyer. Like Pedu's horse who killed the brood of serpents, thus thou, O Soma, slayest every Dasyu.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like Agni loosed amid the forest, fiercely he winneth splendour in the running waters. Like one who fights, the roaring of the mighty, thus Soma Pavamana sends his current.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These Somas passing through the fleecy filter, like rain descending from the clouds of heaven, Have been effused and poured into the beakers, swiftly like rivers running lowly seaward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Flow onward like the potent band of Maruts, like that Celestial Host whom none revileth. Quickly be gracious unto us like waters, like sacrifice victorious, thousand-fashioned.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thine are King Varuna's eternal statutes, lofty and deep, O Soma, is thy glory. All-pure art thou like Mitra the beloved, adorable, like Aryaman, O Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THIS Chariot-horse hath moved along the pathways, and Pavamana flowed like rain from heaven. With us hath Soma with a thousand currents sunk in the wood, upon his Mother's bosom.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: King, he hath clothed him in the robe of rivers, mounted the straightest-going ship of Order. Sped by the Hawk the drop hath waxed in waters: the father drains it, drains the Father's offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They come to him, red, tawny, Lord of Heaven, the watchful Guardian of the meath, the Lion. First, Hero in the fight, he seeks the cattle, and with his eye the Steer is our protector.
