verses.translation: Thence bearing food the Mothers come to meet thee, with food for thee who givest food its increase. These in their altered form again thou meetest. Thou art Invoking Priest in homes of mortals.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Priest of the holy rite, with car that glitters, refulgent Banner of each act of worship, Sharing every God through might and glory, even Agni Guest of men I summon hither.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So Agni stands on earth's most central station, invested in well-decorated garments. Born, red of hue, where men pour out libations, O King, as great High Priest bring the Gods hither.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Over the earth and over heaven, O Agni, thou, Son, hast ever spread above thy Parents. Come, Youthfullest! to those who long to meet thee, and hither bring the Gods, O Mighty Victor.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GLADDEN the yearning Gods, O thou Most Youthful: bring them, O Lord of Seasons, knowing seasons, With all the Priests Celestial, O Agni. Best worshipper art thou of all Invokers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thine is the Herald's, thine the Cleanser's office, thinker art thou, wealth-giver, true to Order. Let us with Svaha offer up oblations, and Agni, worthy God, pay the Gods worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To the Gods' pathway have we travelled, ready to execute what work we may accomplish. Let Agni, for he knows, complete the worship. He is the Priest: let him fix rites and seasons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When we most ignorant neglect the statutes of you, O Deities with whom is knowledge, Wise Agni shall correct our faults and failings, skilled to assign each God his fitting season.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, weak in mind, of feeble understanding, mortals bethink them not of sacrificing, Then shall the prudent and discerning Agni worship the Gods, best worshipper, in season.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Because the Father hath produced thee, Leader of all our solemn rites, their brilliant Banner: So win by worship pleasant homes abounding in heroes, and rich food to nourish all men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou whom the Heaven and Earth, thou whom the Waters, and Tvastar, maker of fair things, created, Well knowing, all along the Fathers' pathway, shine with resplendent light, enkindled, Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O KING, the potent and terrific envoy, kindled for strength, is manifest in beauty. He shines, all-knowing, with his lofty splendour: chasing black Night he comes with white-rayed Morning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Having o'ercome the glimmering Black with beauty, and bringing forth the dame the Great Sire's Daughter, Holding aloft the radiant light of Surya, as messenger of heaven he shines with treasures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Attendant on the Blessed Dame the Blessed hath come: the Lover followeth his Sister. Agni, far-spreading with conspicuous lustre, hath compassed Night with whitely shining garments.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His goings-forth kindle as 'twere high voices the goings of the auspicious Friend of Agni. The rays, the bright beams of the strong-jawed, mighty, adorable Steer are visible as he cometh.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whose radiant splendours flow, like sounds, about us, his who is lofty, brilliant, and effulgent, Who reaches heaven with best and brightest lustres, sportive and piercing even to the summit.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His powers, whose chariot fellies gleam and glitter have loudly roared while, as with teams, he hasted. He, the most Godlike, far-extending envoy, shines with flames ancient, resonant, whitely-shining.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So bring us ample wealth: seat thee as envoy of the two youthful Matrons, Earth and Heaven. Let Agni rapid with his rapid, horses, impetuous with impetuous Steeds, come hither.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee will send praise and bring oblation, as thou hast merited lauds when we invoked thee. A fountain in the desert art thou, Agni, O Ancient King, to man who fain would worship,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou unto whom resort the gathered people, as the kine seek the warm stall, O Most Youthful. Thou art the messenger of Gods and mortals, and goest glorious with thy light between them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Making thee grow as 'twere some noble infant, thy Mother nurtures thee with sweet affection. Over the desert slopes thou passest longing, and seekest, like some beast set free, thy fodder.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Foolish are we, O Wise and free from error: verily, Agni, thou dost know thy grandeur. There lies the form: he moves and licks, and swallows, and, as House-Lord, kisses the Youthful Maiden.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He rises ever fresh in ancient fuel: smoke-bannered, gray, he makes the wood his dwelling. No swimmer, Steer, he presses through the waters, and to his place accordant mortals bear him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like thieves who risk their lives and haunt the forest, the twain with their ten girdles have secured him. This is a new hymn meant for thee, O Agni: yoke as it were thy car with parts that glitter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Homage and prayer are thine, O Jatavedas, and this my song shall evermore exalt thee. Agni, protect our children and descendants, and guard with ever-watchful care our bodies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HE only is the Sea, holder of treasures: born many a time he views the hearts within us. He hides him in the secret couple's bosom. The Bird dwells in the middle of the fountain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Inhabiting one dwelling-place in common, strong Stallions and the Mares have come together. The sages guard the seat of Holy Order, and keep the highest names concealed within them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Holy Pair, of wondrous power, have coupled: they formed the Infant, they who bred produced him. The central point of all that moves and moves not, the while they wove the Sage's thread with insight
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For tracks of Order and refreshing viands attend from ancient times the goodly Infant. Wearing him as a mantle, Earth and Heaven grow strong by food of pleasant drink and fatness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, calling loudly to the Seven red Sisters, hath, skilled in sweet drink, brought them to be looked on. He, born of old, in middle air hath halted, and sought and found the covering robe of Pusan.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Seven are the pathways which the wise have fashioned; to one of these may come the troubled mortal. He standeth in the dwelling of the Highest, a Pillar, on sure ground where paths are parted.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Not Being, Being in the highest heaven, in Aditi's bosom and in Daksa's birthplace, Is Agni, our first-born of Holy Order, the Milch-cow and the Bull in life's beginning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THIS is that Agni, he by whose protection, favour, and help. the singer is successful; Who with the noblest flames of glowing fuel comes forth encompassed with far-spreading lustre.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, the Holy One, the everlasting, who shines far beaming with celestial splendours; He who hath come unto his friends with friendship, like a fleet steed who never trips or stumbles.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who is Lord of all divine oblation, shared by all living men at break of morning, Agni to whom our offerings are devoted, in whom rests he whose car, through might, is scatheless.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Increasing by his strength. while lauds content him, with easy flight unto the Gods he travels. Agni the cheerful Priest, best Sacrificer, balms with his tongue the Gods with whom he mingles.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With songs and adorations bring ye hither Agni who stirs himself at dawn like Indra, Whom sages laud with hymns as Jatavedas of those who wield the sacrificial ladle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In whom all goodly treasures meet together, even as steeds and riders for the booty. Inclining hither bring us help, O Agni, even assistance most desired by Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, at thy birth, when thou hadst sat in glory, thou, Agni, wast the aim of invocations. The Gods came near, obedient to thy summons, and thus attained their rank as chief Protectors.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O AGNI, shared by all men living bring us good luck for sacrifice from earth and heaven. With us be thine intelligence, Wonder Worker! Protect us, God, with thy far-reaching blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These hymns brought forth for thee, O Agni, laud thee for bounteous gifts, with cattle and with horses. Good Lord, when man from thee hath gained enjoyment, by hymns, O nobly born, hath he obtained it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni I deem my Kinsman and my Father, count him my Brother and my Friend for ever. I honour as the face of lofty Agni in heaven the bright and holy light of Surya.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Effectual, Agni, are our prayers for profit. He whom, at home thou, Priest for ever, guardest Is rich in food, drawn by red steeds, and holy: by day and night to him shall all be pleasant.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Men with their arms have generated Agni, helpful as some kind friend, adorned with splendours, And stablished as Invoker mid the people the ancient Priest the sacrifice's lover.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Worship, thyself, O God, the Gods in heaven: what, void of knowledge, shall the fool avail thee? As thou, O God, hast worshipped Gods by seasons, so, nobly-born! to thine own self pay worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, be thou our Guardian and Protector bestow upon us life and vital vigour. Accept, O Mighty One, the gifts we offer, and with unceasing care protect our bodies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI advances with his lofty banner: the Bull is bellowing to the earth and heavens. He hath attained the sky's supremest limits. the Steer hath waxen in the lap of waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Bull, the youngling with the hump, hath frolicked, the strong and never-ceasing Calf hath bellowed. Bringing our offerings to the God's assembly, he moves as Chief in his own dwelling-places.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him who hath grasped his Parents' head, they stablished at sacrifice a wave of heavenly lustre. In his swift flight the red Dawns borne by horses refresh their bodies in the home of Order.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For, Vasu thou precedest every Morning, and still hast been the Twins' illuminator. For sacrifice, seven places thou retainest while for thine own self thou engenderest Mitra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou art the Eye and Guard of mighty Order, and Varuna when to sacrifice thou comest. Thou art the Waters' Child O Jatavedas, envoy of him whose offering thou acceptest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou art the Leader of the rite and region, to which with thine auspicious teams thou leadest, Thy light-bestowing head to heaven thou liftest, making thy tongue the oblationbearer, Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Through his wise insight Trita in the cavern, seeking as ever the Chief Sire's intention, Carefully tended in his Parents' bosom, calling the weapons kin, goes forth to combat.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Well-skilled to use the weapons of his Father, Aptya, urged on by Indra, fought the battle. Then Trita slew the foe seven-rayed, three-headed, and freed the cattle of the Son of Tvastar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lord of the brave, Indra cleft him in pieces who sought to gain much strength and deemed him mighty. He smote his three heads from his body, seizing the cattle of the omniform Son of Tvastar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: YE, Waters, are beneficent: so help ye us to energy That we may look on great delight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give us a portion of the sap, the most auspicious that ye have, Like mothers in their longing love.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To you we gladly come for him to whose abode ye send us on; And, Waters, give us procreant strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Waters. be to us for drink, Goddesses for our aid and bliss: Let them stream to us health and strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: 1 beg the Floods to give us balm, these Queens who rule o'er precious things, And have supreme control of men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Within the Waters-Soma thus hath told me-dwell all balms that heal, And Agni, he who blesseth all.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Waters, teem with medicine to keep my body safe from harm, So that I long may see the Sun.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whatever sin is found in me, whatever evil I have wrought, If I have lied or falsely sworn, Waters, remove it far from me.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Waters I this day have sought, and to their moisture have we come: O Agni, rich in milk, come thou, and with thy splendour cover me.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FAIN would I win my friend to kindly friendship. So may the Sage, come through the air's wide ocean, Remembering the earth and days to follow, obtain a son, the issue of his father.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy friend loves not the friendship which considers her who is near in kindred as stranger. Sons of the mighty Asura, the Heroes, supporters of the heavens, see far around them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, this the Immortals seek of thee with longing, progeny of the sole existing mortal. Then let thy soul and mine be knit together, and as a loving husband take thy consort.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Shall we do now what we ne'er did aforetime? we who spake righteously now talk impurely? Gandharva in the floods, the Dame of Waters-such is our bond, such our most lofty kinship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even in the womb God Tvastar, Vivifier, shaping all forms, Creator, made us consorts. None violates his holy ordinances: that we are his the heavens and earth acknowledge.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who knows that earliest day whereof thou speakest? Who hath beheld it? Who can here declare it? Great is the Law of Varuna and Mitra. What, wanton! wilt thou say to men to tempt them?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I, Yami, am possessed by love of Yama, that I may rest on the same couch beside him. I as a wife would yield me to my husband. Like car-wheels let us speed to meet each other.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They stand not still, they never close their eyelids, those sentinels of Gods who wander round us. Not me-go quickly, wanton, with another, and hasten like a chariot wheel to meet him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Surya's eye with days and nights endow him, and ever may his light spread out before him. In heaven and earth the kindred Pair commingle. On Yam! be the unbrotherly act of Yama.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sure there will come succeeding times when brothers and sisters will do acts unmeet for kinsfolk. Not me, O fair one,-seek another husband, and make thine arm a pillow for thy consort.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Is he a brother when no lord is left her? Is she a sister when Destruction cometh? Forced by my love these many words I utter. Come near, and hold me in thy close embraces.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I will not fold mine arms about thy body: they call it sin when one comes near his sister. Not me,-prepare thy pleasures with another: thy brother seeks not this from thee, O fair one.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Alas! thou art indeed a weakling, Yama we find in thee no trace of heart or spirit. As round the tree the woodbine clings, another will cling about thee girt as with a girdle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Embrace another, Yami; let another, even as the woodbine rings the tree, enfold thee. Win thou his heart and let him win thy fancy, and he shall form with thee a blest alliance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE Bull hath yielded for the Bull the milk of heaven: the Son of Aditi can never be deceived. According to his wisdom Varuna knoweth all: may he, the Holy, hallow times for sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Gandharvi spake: may she, the Lady of the flood, amid the river's roaring leave my heart untouched. May Aditi accomplish all that we desire, and may our eldest Brother tell us this as Chief.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, even this blessed Morning, rich in store of food, splendid, with heavenly lustre, hath shone out for man, Since they, as was the wish of yearning Gods, brought forth that yearning Agni for the assembly as the Priest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And the fleet Falcon brought for sacrifice from afar this flowing Drop most excellent and keen of sight, Then when the Aryan tribes chose as Invoking Priest Agni the Wonder-Worker, and the hymn rose up.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Still art thou kind to him who feeds thee as with grass, and, skilled in sacrifice, offers thee holy gifts. When thou, having received the sage's strengthening food with lauds, after long toil, comest with many more.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Urge thou thy Parents, as a lover ' to delight: the Lovely One desires and craves it from his heart. The priest calls out, the sacrificer shows his skill, the Asura tries his strength, and with the hymn is stirred.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Far-famed is he, the mortal man, O Agni, thou Son of Strength, who hath obtained thy favour. He, gathering power, borne onward by his horses, makes his days lovely in his might and splendour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, Holy Agni, the divine assembly, the sacred synod mid the Gods, is gathered, And when thou, Godlike One, dealest forth treasures, vouchsafe us, too, our portion of the riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hear us, O Agni, in your common dwelling: harness thy rapid car of Amrta. Bring Heaven and Earth, the Deities' Parents, hither: stay with us here, nor from the Gods be distant.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HEAVEN and Earth, first by everlasting Order, speakers of truth, are near enough to hear us, When the God, urging men to worship. sitteth as Priest, assuming all his vital vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As God comprising Gods by Law Eternal, bear, as the Chief who knoweth, our oblation, Smoke-bannered with the fuel, radiant, joyous, better to praise and worship, Priest for ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When the cow's nectar wins the God completely, men here below are heaven's sustainers. All the Gods came to this thy heavenly Yajus which from the motley Pair milked oil and water.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: 1 praise your work that ye may make me prosper: hear, Heaven and Earth, Twain Worlds that drop with fatness. While days and nights go to the world of spirits, here let the Parents with sweet meath refresh us
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hath the King siezed us? How have we offended against his holy ordinance? Who knoweth? For even Mitra mid the Gods is angry there are both song and strength for those who come not.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: 'Tis hard to understand the Immortal's nature, where she who is akin becomes a stranger. Guard ceaselessly, great Agni, him who ponders Yama's name, easy to be comprehended.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They in the synod where the Gods rejoice them, where they are seated in Vivasvan's dwelling, Have given the Moon his beams, the Sun his splendour-the Two unweariedly maintain their brightness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The counsel which the Gods meet to consider, their secret plan,-of that we have no knowledge. There let God Savitar, Aditi, and Mitra proclaim to Varuna that we are sinless.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hear us, O Agni, in your comninn dwelling: harness thy rapid car, the car of Amrta. Bring Heaven and Earth, the Deities' Parents, hither: stay with us here, nor from the Gods be distant.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I YOKE with prayer your ancient inspiration: may the laud rise as on the prince's pathway. All Sons of Immortality shall hear it, all the possessors of celestial natures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When speeding ye came nigh us like twin sisters, religious-hearted votaries brought you forward. Take your place, ye who know your proper station: be near, be very near unto our Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Five paces have I risen from Earth. I follow her who hath four feet with devout observance. This by the Sacred Syllable have I measured: I purify in the central place of Order,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, for God's sake, chose death to be his portion. He chose not, for men's good, a life eternal They sacrificed Brhaspati the Rsi. Yama delivered up his own dear body.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Seven flow to the Youth on whom the Maruts wait: the Sons unto the Father brought the sacrifice. Both these are his, as his they are the Lords of both: both toil; belonging unto both they prosper well.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HONOUR the King with thine oblations, Yama, Vivasvan's Son, who gathers men together, Who travelled to the lofty heights above us, who searches out and shows the path to many.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yama first found for us a place to dwell in: this pasture never can be taken from Us. Men born on earth tread their own paths that lead them whither our ancient Fathers have departed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mitali prospers there with Kavyas, Yama with Angiras' sons, Brhaspati with Rkvans: Exalters of the Gods, by Gods exalted, some joy in praise and some in our oblation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come, seat thee on this bed of grass, O Yama, in company with Angirases and Fathers. Let texts recited by the sages bring thee O King, let this oblation make thee joyful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come, Yama, with the Angirases the Holy, rejoice thee here with children of Virupa. To sit on sacred grass at this our worship, I call Vivasvan, too, thy Father hither.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Our Fathers are Angirases, Navagvas, Atharvans, Bhrgus who deserve the Soma. May these, the Holy, look on us with favour, may we enjoy their gracious loving-kindness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Go forth, go forth upon the ancient pathways whereon our sires of old have gone before us. 'Mere shalt thou look on both the Kings enjoying their sacred food, God Varuna and Yama.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Meet Yama, meet the Fathers, meet the merit of free or ordered acts, in highest heaven. Leave sin and evil, seek anew thy dwelling, and bright with glory wear another body.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Go hence, depart ye, fly in all directions: this place for him the Fathers have provided. Yama bestows on him a place to rest in adorned with days and beams of light and waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Run and outspeed the two dogs, Sarama's offspring, brindled, four-eyed, upon thy happy pathway. Draw nigh then to the gracious-minded Fathers where they rejoice in company with Yama.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And those two dogs of thine, Yama, the watchers, four-eyed, who look on men and guard the pathway,- Entrust this man, O King, to their protection, and with prosperity and health endow him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dark-hued, insatiate, with distended nostrils, Yama's two envoys roam among the People; May they restore to us a fair existence here and to-day, that we may see the sunlight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Yama pour the Soma, bring to Yama consecrated gifts: To Yama sacrifice prepared and heralded by Agni goes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Offer to Yama holy gifts enriched with butter, and draw near: So may he grant that we may live long days of life among the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Offer to Yama, to the King, oblation very rich in meath: Bow down before the Rsis of the ancient times, who made this path in days of old.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Into the six Expanses flies the Great One in Trkadrukas. The Gayatri, the Trstup, all metres in Yama are contained.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MAY they ascend, the lowest, highest, midmost, the Fathers who deserve a share of Soma- May they who have attained the life of spirits, gentle and righteous, aid us when we call them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now let us pay this homage to the Fathers, to those who passed of old and those who followed, Those who have rested in the earthly region, and those who dwell among the Mighty Races.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: 1 have attained the gracious-minded Fathers, I have gained son and progeny from Visnu. They who enjoy pressed juices with oblation seated on sacred grass, come oftenest hither.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fathers who sit on sacred grass, come, help us: these offerings have we made for you; accept them. So come to us with most auspicious favour, and give us health and strength without a trouble.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May they, the Fathers, worthy of the Soma, invited to their favourite oblations. Laid on the sacred grass, come nigh and listen: may they be gracious unto us and bless us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bowing your bended knees and seated southward, accept this sacrifice of ours with favour. Punish us not for any sin, O Fathers, which we through human frailty have committed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lapped in the bosom of the purple Mornings, give riches to the man who brings oblations. Grant to your sons a portion of that treasure, and, present, give them energy, ye Fathers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Our ancient Fathers who deserve the Soma, who came, most noble, to our Soma banquet,- With these let Yama, yearning with the yearning, rejoicing eat our offerings at his pleasure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come to us, Agni, with the gracious Fathers who dwell in glowing light, the very Kavyas, Who thirsted mid the Gods, who hasten hither, oblation winners, theme of singers' praises.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come, Agni, come with countless ancient Fathers, dwellers in light, primeval, God-adorers, Eaters and drinkers of oblations, truthful, who travel with the Deities and Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fathers whom Agni's flames have tasted, come ye nigh: ye kindly leaders, take ye each your proper place. Eat sacrificial food presented on the grass: grant riches with a multitude of hero sons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Agni Jatavedas, when entreated, didst bear the offerings which thou madest fragrant, And give them to the Fathers who did cat them with Svadha. Eat, thou God, the gifts we bring thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Jatavedas, knowest well the number of Fathers who are here and who are absent, Of Fathers whom we know and whom we know not: accept the sacrifice well prepared with portions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who, consumed by fire or not cremated, joy in their offering in the midst of heaven,- Grant them, O Sovran Lord, the world of spirits and their own body, as thy pleasure wills it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Burn him not up, nor quite consume him, Agni: let not his body or his skin be scattered. O Jatavedas, when thou hast matured him, then send him on his way unto the Fathers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When thou hast made him ready, Jatavedas, then do thou give him over to the Fathers. When he attains unto the life that waits him, he shall become the Deities' controller.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Sun receive thine eye, the Wind thy spirit; go, as thy merit is, to earth or heaven. Go, if it be thy lot, unto the waters; go, make thine home in plants with all thy members.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy portion is the goat: with heat consume him: let thy fierce flame, thy glowing splendour, burn him With thine auspicious forms, o Jatavedas, bear this man to the region of the pious.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Again, O Agni, to the Fathers send him who, offered in thee, goes with our oblations. Wearing new life let him increase his offspring: let him rejoin a body, Jatavedas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What wound soe'er the dark bird hath inflicted, the emmet, or the serpent, or the jackal, May Agni who devoureth all things heal it and Soma who hath passed into the Brahmans.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Shield thee with flesh against the flames of Agni, encompass thee about with fat and marrow, So will the Bold One, eager to attack thee with fierce glow fail to girdle and consume thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Forbear, O Agni, to upset this ladle: the Gods and they who merit Soma love it. This ladle, this which serves the Gods to drink from, in this the Immortal Deities rejoice them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: 1 send afar flesh eating Agni, bearing off stains may he depart to Yama's subjects. But let this other Jatavedas carry oblation to the Gods, for he is skillful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I choose as God for Father-worship Agni, flesh-eater, who hath past within your dwelling, While looking on this other Jatavedas. Let him light flames in the supreme assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With offerings meet let Agni bring the Fathers who support the Law. Let him announce oblations paid to Fathers and to Deities.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Right gladly would we set thee down, right gladly make thee burn and glow. Gladly bring yearning Fathers nigh to cat the food of sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Cool, Agni, and again refresh the spot which thou hast scorched and burnt. Here let the water-lily grow, and tender grass and leafy herb.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O full of coolness, thou cool Plant, full of fresh moisture, freshening Herb, Come hither with the female frog: fill with delight this Agni here.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: TVASTAR prepares the bridal of his Daughter: all the world hears the tidings and assembles. But Yama's Mother, Spouse of great Vivasvan, vanished as she was carried to her dwelling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From mortal men they hid the Immortal Lady, made one like her and gave her to Vivasvan. Saranyu brought to him the Asvin brothers, and then deserted both twinned pairs of children.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Guard of the world, whose cattle ne'er are injured, may Pusan bear thee hence, for he hath knowledge. May he consign thee to these Fathers' keeping, and to the gracious Gods let Agni give thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Ayu, giver of all life, protect thee, and bear thee forward on the distant pathway. Thither let Savitar the God transport thee, where dwell the pious who have passed-before thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pusan knows all these realms: may he conduct us by ways that are most free from fear and danger. Giver of blessings, glowing, all-heroic, may he, the wise and watchful, go before us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pusan was born to move on distant pathways, on the road far from earth and far from heaven. To both most wonted places of assembly he travels and returns with perfect knowledge.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The pious call Sarasvati, they worship Sarasvati while sacrifice proceedeth. The pious called Sarasvati aforetime. Sarasvati send bliss to him who giveth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sarasvati, who camest with the Fathers, with them rejoicing thee in our oblations, Seated upon this sacred grass be joyful, and give us strengthening food that brings no sickness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, called on as Sarasvati by Fathers who come right forward to our solemn service, Give food and wealth to present sacrificers, a portion, worth a thousand, of refreshment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Mother Floods shall make us bright and shining, cleansers of holy oil, with oil shall cleanse us: For, Goddesses, they bear off all defilement: I, rise up from them purified and brightened.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Through days of earliest date the Drop descended on this place and on that which was before it. I offer up, throughout the seven oblations, the Drop which still to one same place is moving.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Drop that falls, thy stalk which arms have shaken, which from the bosom of the press hath fallen, Or from the Adhvaryu's purifying filter, I offer thee with heart and cry of Vasat!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That fallen Drop of thine, the stalk which from the ladle fell away, This present God Brhaspati shall pour it forth to make us rich.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The plants of earth are rich in milk, and rich in milk is this my speech; And rich in milk the essence of the Waters: make me pure therewith.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Go hence, O Death, pursue thy special pathway apart from that which Gods are wont to travel. To thee I say it who hast eyes and hearest: Touch not our offspring, injure not our heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As ye have come effacing Mrtyu's footstep, to further times prolonging your existence, May ye be rich in children and possessions. cleansed, purified, and meet for sacrificing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Divided from the dead are these, the living: now be our calling on the Gods successful. We have gone forth for dancing and for laughter, to further times prolonging our existence.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here I erect this rampart for the living; let none of these, none other, reach this limit. May they survive a hundred lengthened autumns, and may they bury Death beneath this mountain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As the days follow days in close succession, as with the seasons duly come the seasons, As each successor fails not his foregoer, so form the lives of these, O great Ordainer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Live your full lives up! find old age delightful, all of you striving one behind the other. May Tvastar, maker of fair things, be gracious and lengthen out the days of your existence.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let these unwidowed dames with noble husbands adorn themselves with fragrant balm and unguent. Decked with fair jewels, tearless, free from sorrow, first let the dames go up to where he lieth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rise, come unto the world of life, O woman: come, he is lifeless by whose side thou liest. Wifehood with this thy husband was thy portion, who took thy hand and wooed thee as a lover.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From his dead hand I take the bow be carried, that it may be our power and might and glory. There art thou, there; and here with noble heroes may we o'ercome all hosts that fight against us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Betake thee to the lap of Earth the Mother, of Earth far-spreading, very kind and gracious. Young Dame, wool-soft unto the guerdon giver, may she preserve thee from Destruction's bosom.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Heave thyself, Earth, nor press thee downward heavily: afford him easy access, gently tending him. Cover him, as a mother wraps her skirt about her child, O Earth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now let the heaving earth be free from motion: yea,- let a thousand clods remain above him. Be they to him a home distilling fatness, here let them ever be his place of refuge.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I stay the earth from thee, while over thee I place this piece of earth. May I be free from injury. Here let the Fathers keep this pillar firm for thee, and there let Yama make thee an abiding-place.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even as an arrow's feathers, they have set me on a fitting day. The fit word have I caught and held as 'twere a courser with the rein.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: TURN, go not farther on your way: visit us, O ye Wealthy Ones. Agni and Soma, ye who bring riches again, secure us wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Make these return to us again, bring them beside us once again. May. Indra give them back to us, and Agni drive them hither-ward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let them return to us again: under this herdsman let them feed. Do thou, O Agni, keep them here, and let the wealth we have remain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: 1 call upon their herdsman, him who knoweth well their coming nigh, Their parting and their home-return, and watcheth their approach and rest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, let the herdsman, too, return, who marketh well their driving-forth; Marketh their wandering away, their turning back and coming home.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Home-leader, lead them home to us; Indra, restore to us our kine: We will rejoice in them alive.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: 1 offer you on every side butter and milk and strengthening food. May all the Holy Deities pour down on us a flood of wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O thou Home-leader, lead them home, restore them thou who bringest home. Four are the quarters of the earth; from these bring back to us our kine,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SEND unto us a good and happy mind.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I worship Agni, Youthfullest of Gods, resistless, Friend of laws; Under whose guard and heavenly light the Spotted seek the Mother's breast:
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whom with their mouth they magnify, bannered with flame and homed in light. He glitters with his row of teeth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Kind, Furtherer of men, he comes, when he hath reached the ends of heaven, Sage, giving splendour to the clouds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To taste man's offerings, he, the Strong, hath risen erect at sacrifice: Fixing his dwelling he proceeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here are oblation, worship, rest: rapidly comes his furtherance. To sword-armed Agni come the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With service for chief bliss I seek the Lord of Sacrifice, Agni, whom They call the Living, Son of Cloud.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Blest evermore be all the men who come from us, who magnify Agni with sacrificial gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The path he treads is black and white and red, and striped, and brown, crimson, and glorious. His sire begat him bright with hues of gold.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thus with his thoughts, O Son of Strength, O Agni, hath Vimada, accordant with the Immortals, Offered thee hymns, soliciting thy favour. Thou hast brought all food, strength, a prosperous dwelling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WITH offerings of our own we choose thee, Agni, as Invoking Priest, For sacrifice with trimmed grass,-at your glad carouse-piercing and brightly shining. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The wealthy ones adorn thee, they who bring us horses as their gift: The sprinkling ladle, Agni,-at your glad carouse -and glowing offering taste thee. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The holy statutes rest by thee, as 'twere with ladles that o'erflow. Black and white-gleaming colours,-at your glad carouse-all glories thou assumest. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, what thou deemest wealth, Victorious and Immortal One! Bring thou to give us vigour,-at your glad carouse -splendid at sacrifices. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Skilled in all lore is Agni, he whom erst Atharvan brought to life. He was Vivasvan's envoy, at your glad carouse-the well-loved friend of Yama, Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: At sacrifices they adore thee, Agni, when the rite proceeds. All fair and lovely treasures-at your glad carouse-thou givest him who offers. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Men, Agni, have established thee as welcome Priest at holy rites, Thee whose face shines with butter,-at your glad carouse-bright, with eyes most observant. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wide and aloft thou spreadest thee, O Agni, with thy brilliant flame. A Bull art thou when bellowing,-at your glad carouse-thou dost impregn the Sisters. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHERE is famed Indra heard of? With what folk is he renowned to-day as Mitra is,- Who in the home of Rsis and in secret is extolled with song?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even here is Indra famed, and among us this day the glorious Thunderer is praised, He who like Mitra mid the folk hath won complete and full renown.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who is Sovran Lord of great and perfect strength, exerter of heroic might, Who bears the fearless thunder as a father bears his darling son.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Harnessing to thy car, as God, two blustering Steeds Of the Wind-God, O Thunderer, That speed along the shining path, thou making ways art glorified.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even to these dark Steeds of Wind thou of thyself hast come to ride, Of which no driver may be found, none, be he God or mortal man.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When ye approach, men ask you, thee and Usana: Why come ye to our dwelling-place? Why are ye come to mortal man from distant realms of earth and heaven?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra, thou shalt speak us fair: our holy prayer is offered up. We pray to thee for help as thou didst strike the monster Susna dead.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Around us is the Dasyu, riteless, void of sense, inhuman, keeping alien laws. Baffle, thou Slayer of the foe, the weapon which this Dasa wields.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hero with Heroes, thou art ours: yea, strong are they whom thou dost help. In many a place are thy full gifts, and men, like vassals, sing thy praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Urge thou these heroes on to slay the enemy, brave Thunderer! in the fight with swords. Even when hid among the tribes of Sages numerous as stars.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Swift come those gifts of thine whose hand is prompt to rend and burn, O Hero Thunder-armed: As thou with thy Companions didst destroy the whole of Susna's brood.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let not thine excellent assistance come to us, O Hero Indra, profitless. May we, may we enjoy the bliss of these thy favours, Thunderer!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May those soft impulses of thine, O Indra, be fruitful and innocent to us. May we know these whose treasures are like those of milch-kine, Thunderer!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That Earth, through power of knowing things that may be known, handless and footless yet might thrive, Thou slewest, turning to the right, Susna for every living man.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drink, drink the Soma, Hero Indra; be not withheld as thou art good, O Treasure-giver. Preserve the singers and our liberal princes, and make us wealthy with abundant riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: INDRA, whose right hand wields the bolt, we worship, driver of Bay Steeds seeking sundered courses. Shaking his beard with might he hath arisen, casting his weapons forth and dealing bounties.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The treasure which his Bay Steeds found at sacrifice,-this wealth made opulent Indra slayer of the foe. Rbhu, Rbhuksan, Vaja-he is Lord of Might. The Dasa's very name I utterly destroy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, with the Princes, Maghavari, famed of old, comes nigh the thunderbolt of gold, and the Controller's car Which his two Tawny Coursers draw, then Indra is the Sovran Lord of power whose glory spreads afar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With him too is this rain of his that comes like herds: Indra throws drops of moisture on his yellow beard. When the sweet juice is shed he seeks the pleasant place, and stirs the worshipper as wind disturbs the wood.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We laud and praise his several deeds of valour who, father like, with power hath made us stronger; Who with his voice slew many thousand wicked ones who spake in varied manners with contemptuous cries.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, the Vimadas have formed for thee a laud, copious, unparalleled, for thee Most Bountiful. We know the good we gain from him the Mighty One when we attract him as a herdsman calls the kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ne'er may this bond of friendship be dissevered, the Rsi Vimada's and thine, O Indra. We know thou carest for us as a brother with us, O God, be thine auspicious friendship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O INDRA, drink this Soma, pressed out in the mortar, full of sweets. Send down to us great riches,-at your glad carouse-in thousands, O Most healthy. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee with sacrifices, with oblations, and with lauds we come. Lord of all strength and power, grant-at your glad carouse-the best choice worthy treasure. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou who art Lord of precious boons, inciter even of the churl. Guardian of singers, Indra,-at your glad carouse-save us from woe and hatred. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong, Lords of Magic power, ye Twain churned the united worlds apart, When ye, implored by Vimada, Nasatyas, forced apart the pair.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When the united pair were rent asunder all the Gods complained. The Gods to the Nasatyas cried, Bring these together once again.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sweet be my going forth, and rich in sweets be my approach to home. So, through your Deity, both Gods, enrich us with all pleasantness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SEND us a good and happy mind, send energy and mental power. Then-at your glad carouse-let men joy in thy love, Sweet juice! as kine in pasture. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: rn all thy forms, O Soma, rest thy powers that influence the heart. So also these my longings-at your glad carouse-spread themselves seeking riches. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even if, O Soma, I neglect thy laws through my simplicity, Be gracious-at your glad carouse-as sire to son. Preserve us even from slaughter. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Our songs in concert go to thee as streams of water to the wells. Soma, that we may live, grant-at your glad carouse-full powers of mind, like beakers. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Soma, through thy might who art skillful and strong, these longing men, These sages, have thrown open-at your glad carouse-the stall of kine and horses. Thou art waxing great
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Our herds thou guardest, Soma, and the moving world spread far and wide. Thou fittest them for living,-at your glad carouse-looking upon all beings. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: On all sides, Soma, be to us a Guardian ne'er to be deceived. King, drive away our foemen-at your glad carouse:-let not the wicked rule us. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be watchful, Soma, passing wise, to give us store of vital strength. More skilled than man to guide us,-at your glad carouse-save us from harm and sorrow. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Chief slayer of our foemen, thou, Indu, art Indra's gracious Friend, When warriors invoke him-at your glad carouse -in fight, to win them offspring. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Victorious is this gladdening drink: to Indra dear it grows in strength. This-at your glad carouse -enhanced the mighty hymn of the great sage Kaksivan. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This to the sage who offers gifts brings power that comes from wealth in kine. This, better than the seven, hath-at your glad carouse-furthered the blind, the cripple. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FORWARD upon their way proceed the ready teams, the lovely songs. Further them glorious Pusan with yoked chariot, and the Mighty Twain!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With sacred hymns let this man here, this singer, win the God to whom Belong this majesty and might. He hath observed our eulogies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pusan the Strong hath knowledge of sweet praises even as Indu hath. He dews our corn with moisture, he bedews the pasture of our kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We will bethink ourselves of thee, O Pusan, O thou God, as One. Who brings fulfilment of our hymns, and stirs the singer and the sage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: joint-sharer of each sacrifice, the driver of the chariot steeds; The Rsi who is good to man, the singer's Friend and faithful Guard.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: One who is Lord of Suca, Lord of Suca caring for herself: Weaving the raiment of the sheep and making raiment beautiful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The mighty Lord of spoil and wealth, Strong Friend of all prosperity; He with light movement shakes his beard, lovely and ne'er to be deceived.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Pusan, may those goats of thine turn hitherward thy chariot-pole. Friend of all suppliants; art thou, born in old time, and arm and sure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the majestic Pusan speed our chariot with his power and might. May he increase our store of wealth and listen to this call of ours.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THIS, singer, is my firm determination, to aid the worshipper who pours the Soma. I slay the man who brings no milk oblation, unrighteous, powerful, the truth's perverter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Then Will I, when I lead my friends to battle against the radiant persons of the godless, Prepare for thee at home a vigorous bullock, and pour for thee the fifteen-fold strong juices.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I know not him who sayeth and declareth that he hath slain the godless in the battle. Soon as they see the furious combat raging, men speak forth praises of my vigorous horses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: While yet my deeds of might were unrecorded, all passed for Maghavans though I existed. The potent one who dwelt in peace I conquered, grasped by the foot and slew him on the mountain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: None hinder me in mine heroic exploits, no, not the mountains when I will and purpose. Even the deaf will tremble at my roaring, and every day will dust be agitated.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To see the Indraless oblation-drinkers, mean offerers, o'ertaken by destruction! Then shall the fellies of my car pass over those who have blamed my joyous Friend and scorned him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou wast, thou grewest to full vital vigour: an earlier saw, a later one shall see thee. Two canopies, as 'twere, are round about him who reacheth to the limit of this region.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The freed kine eat the barley of the pious. 1 saw them as they wandered with the herdsman. The calling of the pious rang around them. What portion will these kine afford their owner?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When we who cat the grass of men are gathered I am with barley-eaters in the corn-land. There shall the captor yoke the yokeless bullock, and he who hath been yoked seek one to loose him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: There wilt thou hold as true my spoken purpose, to bring together quadrupeds. and bipeds. I will divide, without a fight, his riches who warreth here, against the Bull, with women.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When a man's daughter hath been ever eyeless, who, knowing, will be wroth with her for blindness? Which of the two will loose on him his anger-the man who leads her home or he who woos her?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How many a maid is pleasing to the suitor who fain would marry for her splendid riches? If the girl be both good and fair of feature, she finds, herself, a friend among the people.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His feet have grasped: he eats the man who meets him. Around his head he sets the head for shelter. Sitting anear and right above he smites us, and follows earth that lies spread out beneath him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: High, leafless, shadowless, and swift is Heaven: the Mother stands, the Youngling, loosed, is feeding. Loud hath she lowed, licking Another's offspring. In what world hath the Cow laid down her udder?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Seven heroes from the nether part ascended, and from the upper part came eight together. Nine from behind came armed with winnowing-baskets: ten from the front pressed o'er the rock's high ridges.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: One of the ten, the tawny, shared in common, they send to execute their final purpose. The Mother carries on her breast the Infant of noble form and soothes it while it knows not.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Heroes dressed with fire the fatted weather: the dice were thrown by way of sport and gaming. Two reach the plain amid the heavenly waters, hallowing and with means of purifying.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Crying aloud they ran in all directions: One half of them will cook, and not the other. To me hath Savitar, this God, declared it: He will perform, whose food is wood and butter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I saw a troop advancing from the distance moved, not by wheels but their own God-like nature. The Friendly One seeks human generations, destroying, still new bands of evil beings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These my two Bulls, even Pramara's, are harnessed: drive them not far; here let them often linger. The waters even shall aid him to his object, and the all-cleansing Sun who is above us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is the thunderbolt which often whirleth down from the lofty misty realm of Surya. Beyond this realm there is another glory so through old age they pass and feel no sorrow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bound fast to,every tree the cow is lowing, and thence the man-consuming birds are flying, Then all this world, though pressing juice for Indra and strengthening the Rsi, is affrighted.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In the Gods' mansion stood the first-created, and from their separation came the later. Three warm the Earth while holding stores of water, and Two of these convey the murmuring moisture.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is thy life: and do thou mark and know it. As such, hide not thyself in time of battle. He manifests the light and hides the vapour: his foot is never free from robes that veil it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now all my other friends are here assembled: my Sire-in-law alone hath not come hither. So might he eat the grain and drink the Soma, and, satisfied, return unto; his dwelling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Loud belloweth the Bull whose horns are sharpened: upon the height above earth's breadth he standeth. That man I guard and save in all his troubles who fills my flanks when he hath shed the Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Men with the stone press out for thee, O Indra, strong, gladdening Soma, and thereof thou drinkest. Bulls they dress for thee, and of these thou eatest when, Maghavan, with food thou art invited.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Resolve for me, O singer, this my riddle: The rivers send their swelling water backward: The fox steals up to the approaching lion: the jackal drives the wild-boar from the brushwood.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How shall I solve this riddle, I, the simple, declare the thought of thee the Wise and Mighty? Tell us, well knowing, as befits the season: Whitherward is thy prosperous car advancing?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thus do they magnify me, me the mighty higher than even high heaven is my car-pole. I all at once demolish many thousands: my Sire begot me with no foe to match me.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, and the Gods have known me also, Indra, as mighty, fierce and strong in every exploit. Exulting with the bolt I slaughtered Vrtra, and for the offerer open with might the cow-stall.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Deities approached, they carried axes; splitting the wood they came with their attendants. They laid good timber in the fire-receivers, and burnt the grass up where they found it growing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The hare hath swallowed up the opposing razor: I sundered with a clod the distant mountain. The great will I make subject to the little: the calf shall wax in strength and cat the bullock.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: There hath the strong-winged eagle left his talon, as a snared lion leaves the trap that caught him. Even the wild steer in his thirst is captured: the leather strap still holds his foot entangled.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So may the leather strap their foot entangle who fatten on the viands of the Brahman. They all devour the bulls set free to wander, while they themselves destroy their bodies' vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They were well occupied with holy duties who sped in person with their lauds to Soma. Speaking like man, mete to us wealth and booty: in heaven thou hast the name and fame of Hero.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As sits the young bird on the tree rejoicing, ye, swift Pair, have been roused by clear laudation, Whose Herald-Priest through many days is Indra, earth's Guardian, Friend of men, the best of Heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we, when this Dawn and the next dance hither, be thy best servants, most heroic Hero! Let the victorious car with triple splendour bring hitherward the hundred chiefs with Kutsa.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What was the gladdening draught that pleased thee, Indra? Speed through our doors to songs, for thou art mighty. Why comest thou to me, what gift attracts thee? Fain would I bring thee food most meet to offer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, what fame hath one like thee mid heroes? With what plan wilt thou act? Why hast thou sought us? As a true Friend, Wide-Strider! to sustain us, since food absorbs the thought of each among us.
