verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Within my mouth, Brhaspati, deposit speech lucid, vigorous, and free from weakness, Thereby to win for Santanu the rain-fall. The meath-rich drop from heaven hath passed within it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let the sweet drops descend on us, O Indra: give us enough to lade a thousand wagons. Sit to thy Hotar task; pay worship duly, and serve the Gods, Devapi, with oblation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Knowing the God's good-will, Devapi, Rsi, the son of Rstisena, sate as Hotar. He hath brought down from heaven's most lofty summit the ocean of the rain, celestial waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Gathered together in that highest ocean, the waters stood by deities obstructed. They hurried down set free by Arstisena, in gaping clefts, urged onward by Devapi.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When as chief priest for Santanu, Devapi, chosen for Hotar's duty, prayed beseeching, Graciously pleased Brhaspati vouchsafed him a voice that reached the Gods and won the waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni whom Devapi Arstisena, the mortal man, hath kindled in his glory, Joying in him with all the Gods together, urge on the sender of the rain, Parjanya.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All ancient Rsis with their songs approached thee, even thee, O Much-invoked, at sacrifices. We have provided wagon-loads in thousands: come to the solemn rite, Lord of Red Horses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The wagon-loads, the nine-and-ninety thousand, these have been offered up to thee, O Agni. Hero, with these increase thy many bodies, and, stimulated, send us rain from heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give thou these ninety thousand loads, O Agni, to Indra, to the Bull, to be his portion. Knowing the paths which Deities duly travel, set mid the Gods in heaven Aulana also.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, drive afar our foes, our troubles chase malady away and wicked demons. From this air-ocean, from the lofty heavens, send down on us a mighty flood of waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHAT Splendid One, Loud-voiced, Far striding, dost thou, well knowing, urge us to exalt with praises? What give we him? When his might dawned, he fashioned the Vrtra-slaying bolt, and sent us waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He goes to end his work with lightning flashes: wide is the seat his Asura glory gives him. With his Companions, not without his Brother, he quells Saptatha's magic devices.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: On most auspicious path he goes to battle he toiled to win heaven's light, full fain to gain it; He seized the hundred-gated castle's treasure by craft, unchecked, and slew the lustful demons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fighting for kine, the prize of war, and I roaming among the berd be brings the young streams hither, Where, footless, joined, without a car to bear them, with jars for steeds, they pour their flood like butter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bold, unsolicited for wealth, with Rudras he came, the Blameless, having left his dwelling, Came, seized the food of Vamra and his consort, and left the couple weeping and unsheltered.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lord of the dwelling, he subdued the demon who roared aloud, six-eyed and triple-headed. Trta, made stronger by the might he lent him, struck down the boar with shaft whose point was iron.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He raised himself on high and shot his arrow against the guileful and oppressive foeman. Strong, glorious, manliest, for us he shattered the forts of Nabus when he slew the Dasyus.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, like a cloud that rains upon the pasture, hath found for us the way to dwell in safety. When the Hawk comes in body to the Soma, armed with his iron claws he slays the Dasyus.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He with his potent Friends gave up the mighty, gave Gusnia up to Kutsa for affliction. He led the lauded Kavi, he delivered Atka as prey to him and to his heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, with his Gods who love mankind, the Wondrous, giving like Varuna who works with magic, Was known, yet young as guardian of the seasons; and he quelled Araru, four-footed demon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Through lauds of him hath Ausija Rjisvan burst, with the Mighty's aid, the stall of Pipru. When the saint pressed the juice and shone as singer, he seized the forts and with his craft subdued them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So, swiftly Asura, for exaltation, hath the great Vamraka come nigh to Indra. He will, when supplicated, bring him blessing: he hath brought all, food, strength, a happy dwelling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be, like thyself, O Indra, strong for our delight: here lauded, aid us, Maghavan, drinker of the juice. Savitar with the Gods protect us: hear ye Twain. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring swift, for offering, the snare that suits the time, to the pure-drinker Vayu, roaring as he goes, To him who hath approached the draught of shining milk. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Savitar the God send us full life, to each who sacrifices, lives aright and pours the juice That we with simple hearts may wait upon the Gods. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Indra evermore be gracious unto us, and may King Soma meditate our happiness, Even as men secure the comfort of a friend. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra hath given the body with its song and strength: Brhaspati, thou art the lengthener of life. The sacrifice is Manu, Providence, our Sire. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra possesseth might celestial nobly formed: the singer in the hotise is Agni, prudent Sage. lie is the sacrifice in synod, fair, most near. We ask for freedom and complete felicity,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Not often have we sinned against you secretly, nor, Vasus, have we openly provoked the Gods. Not one of its, ye Gods, hath worn an alien shape. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Savitar remove from us our malady, and may the Mountains keep it far away from where The press-stone as it sheds the meath rings loudly forth. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye Vasus, let the stone, the presser stand erect: avert all enmities and keep them far remote. Our guard to be adored is Savitar this God. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Eat strength and fatness in the pasture, kine, who are balmed at the reservoir and at the seat of Law. So let your body be our body's medicine. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The singer fills the spirit: all mens, love hath he. Indra takes kindly care of those who pour the juice. For his libation is the heavenly udder full. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wondrous thy spirit-filling light, triumphant; thy hosts save from decay and are resistless. The pious votary by straightest pathway speeds to possess the best of all the cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WAKE with one mind, my friends, and kindle Agni, ye who are many and who dwell together. Agni and Dadhikras and Dawn the Goddess, you, Gods with Indra, I call down to help us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Make pleasant hymns, spin out your songs and praises: build ye a ship equipped with oars for transport. Prepare the implements, make all things ready, and let the sacrifice, my friends, go forward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lay on the yokes, and fasten well the traces: formed is the furrow, sow the seed within it. Through song may we find bearing fraught with plenty: near to the ripened grain approach the sickle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wise, through desire of bliss from Gods, the skillful bind the traces fast, And lay the yokes on either side.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Arrange the buckets in their place securely fasten on the straps. We will pour forth the well that hath a copious stream, fair-flowing well that never fails.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I pour the water from the well with pails prepared and goodly straps, Unfailing, full, with plenteous stream.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Refresh the horses, win the prize before you: equip a chariot fraught with happy fortune. Pour forth the well with stone wheel, wooden buckets, the drink of heroes, with the trough for armour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Prepare the cow-stall, for there drink your heroes: stitch ye the coats of armour, wide and many. Make iron forts, secure from all assailants let not your pitcher leak: stay it securely.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hither, for help, I turn the holy heavenly mind of you the Holy Gods, that longs for sacrifice. May it pour milk for us, even as a stately cow who, having sought the pasture, yields a thousand streams.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pour golden juice within the wooden vessel: with stone-made axes fashion ye and form it. Embrace and compass it with tenfold girdle, and to both chariot-poles attach the car-horse.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Between both poles the car-horse goes pressed closely, as in his dwelling moves the doubly-wedded. Lay in the wood the Soviran of the Forest, and sink the well although ye do not dig it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra is he, O men, who gives us happiness: sport, urge the giver of delight to win us strength Bring quickly down, O priests, hither to give us aid, to drink the Soma, Indra Son of Nistigri.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FOR thee may Indra boldly speed the car that works on either side. Favour us, Much-invoked! in this most glorious fight against the raiders of our wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Loose in the wind the woman's robe was streaming what time she won a car-load worth a thousand. The charioteer in fight was Mudgalani: she Indra's dart, heaped up the prize of battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra, cast thy bolt among assailants who would slaughter us: The weapon both of Dasa and of Arya foe keep far away, O Maghavan.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The bull in joy had drunk a lake of water. His shattering horn encountered an opponent. Swiftly, in vigorous strength, eager for glory, he stretched his forefeet, fain to win and triumph.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They came anear the bull; they made him thunder, made him pour rain down ere the fight was ended. And Mudgala thereby won in the contest well-pastured kine in hundreds and in thousands.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In hope of victory that bull was harnessed: Kesi the driver urged him on with shouting. As he ran swiftly with the car behind him his lifted heels pressed close on Mudgalani.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Deftly for him he stretched the car-pole forward, guided the bull thereto and firmly yoked him. Indra vouchsafed the lord of cows his favour: with mighty steps the buffalo ran onward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Touched by the goad the shaggy beast went nobly, bound to the pole by the yoke's thong of leather. Performing deeds of might for many people, he, looking on the cows, gained strength and vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here look upon this mace, this bull's companion, now lying midway on the field of battle. Therewith hath Mudgala in ordered contest won for cattle for himself, a hundred thousand.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Far is the evil: who hath here beheld it? Hither they bring the bull whom they are yoking.. To this they give not either food or water. Reaching beyond the pole it gives directions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like one forsaken, she hath found a husband, and teemed as if her breast were full and flowing. With swiftly-racing chariot may we conquer, and rich and blessed be our gains in battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Indra, art the mark whereon the eyes of all life rest, when thou, A Bull who drivest with thy bull, wilt win the race together with thy weakling friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SWIFT, rapidly striking, like a bull who sharpens his horns, terrific, stirring up the people, With eyes that close not, bellowing, Sole Hero, Indra. subdued at once a hundred armies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With him loud-roaring, ever watchful, Victor, bold, hard to overthrow, Rouser of battle, Indra. the Strong, whose hand bears arrows, conquer, ye warriors, now, now vanquish in the combat.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He rules with those who carry shafts and quivers, Indra who with his band rings hosts together, Foe-conquering, strong of arm, the Soma-drinker, with mighty bow, shooting with well-laid arrows.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Brhaspati, fly with thy chariot hither, slayer of demons, driving off our foemen. Be thou protector of our cars, destroyer, victor in battle, breaker-up of armies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Conspicuous by thy strength, firm, foremost fighter, mighty and fierce, victorious, all-subduing, The Son of Conquest, passing men and heroes, kine-winner, mount thy conquering car, O Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Cleaver of stalls, kine-winner, armed with thunder, who quells an army and with might destroys it.- Follow him, brothers! quit yourselves like heroes, and like this Indra show your zeal and courage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Piercing the cow-stalls with surpassing vigour, Indra, the pitiless Hero, wild with anger, Victor in fight, unshaken and resistless, may he protect our armies in our battles.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra guide these: Brhaspati precede them, the guerdon, and the sacrifice, and Soma; And let the banded Maruts march in forefront of heavenly hosts that conquer and demolish.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ours be the potent host of mighty Indra, King Varuna, and Maruts, and Adityas. Uplifted is the shout of Gods who conquer high-minded Gods who cause the worlds to tremble.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bristle thou up, O Maghavan, our weapons: excite the spirits of my warring heroes. Urge on the strong steeds' might, O Vrtra-slayer, and let the din of conquering cars go upward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Indra aid us when our flags are gathered: victorious be the arrows of our army. May our brave men of war prevail in battle. Ye Gods, protect us in the shout of onset.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bewildering the senses of our foemen, seize thou their bodies and depart, O Apva. Attack them, set their hearts on fire and burn them: so let our foes abide in utter darkness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Advance, O heroes, win the day. May Indra be your sure defense. Exceeding mighty be your arms, that none may wound or injure you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma hath flowed for thee, Invoked of mat Speed to our sacrifice with both thy Coursers. To thee have streamed the songs or mighty singers, imploring, Indra, drink of our libation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drink of the juice which men have washed in waters, and fill thee full, O Lord of Tawny Horses. O Indra, hearer of the laud, with Soma which stones have mixed for thee enhance thy rapture.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To make thee start, a strong true draught I offer to thee, the Bull, O thou whom Bay Steeds carry. Here take delight, O Indra, in our voices while thou art hymned with power and all our spirit.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Mighty Indra, through thine aid, thy prowess, obtaining life, zealous, and skilled in Order, Men in the house who share the sacred banquet stand singing praise that brings them store of children.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Through thy directions, Lord of Tawny Coursers, thine who art firm, splendid, and blest, the people Obtain most liberal aid for their salvation, and praise thee, Indra, through thine excellencies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lord of the Bays, come with thy two Bay Horses, come to our prayers, to drink the juice of Soma. To thee comes sacrifice which thou acceptest: thou, skilled in holy rites, art he who giveth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him of a thousand powers, subduing foemen, Maghavan praised with hymns and pleased with Soma,- Even him our songs approach, resistless Indra: the adorations of the singer laud him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The way to bliss for Gods and man thou foundest, Indra, seven lovely floods, divine, untroubled, Wherewith thou, rending forts, didst move the ocean, and nine-and-ninety flowing streams of water.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou from the curse didst free the mighty Waters, and as their only God didst watch and guard them. O Indra, cherish evermore thy body with those which thou hast won in quelling Vrtra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Heroic power and noble praise is Indra yea, the song worships him invoked of many. Vrtra he quelled, and gave men room and freedom: Gakra, victorious, hath conquered armies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Call we on Maghayan, auspicious Indra. best Hero in this fight where spoil is gathered, The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vrtras, wins and gathers riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHEN, Vasu, wilt thou love the laud? Now let the channel bring the stream. The juice is ready to ferment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He whose two Bay Steeds harnessed well, swerving, pursue the Bird's tail-plumes, With Rowing manes, like heaven and earth, he is the Lord with power to give.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bereft of skill is Indra, if, like some outwearied man he fears The sinner, when the Mighty hath prepared himself for victory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra with these drives round, until he meets with one to worship him: Indra is Master of the pair who snort and swerve upon their way.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Borne onward by the long-maned Steeds who stretch themselves as 'twere for food, The God who wears the helm defends them with his jaws.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Mighty sang with Lofty Ones: the Hero fashioned with his strength, Like skillful Matarisvan with his power and might,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The bolt, which pierced at once the vitals of the Dasyu easy to be slain, With jaw uninjured like the wondrous firmament.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Grind off our sins: with song will we conquer the men who sing no hymns: Not easily art thou pleased with prayerless sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When threefold flame burns high for thee, to rest on poles of sacrifice, Thou with the living joyest in the self-bright Ship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy glory was the speckled cup, thy glory was the flawless scoop. Wherewith thou pourest into thy receptacle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As hundreds, O Immortal God, have sung to thee, so hath Sumitra, yea, Durmitra praised thee here, What time thou holpest Kutsa's son, when Dasyus fell, yea, holpest Kutsa's darling when the Dasyus died.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THIS very thing ye Twain hold as your object: ye weave your songs as skillful men weave garments. That ye may come united have I waked you: ye spread out food like days of lovely weather.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like two plough-bulls ye move along in traces, and seek like eager guests your bidder's banquet. Ye are like glorious envoys mid the people: like bulls, approach the place where ye are watered.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like the two pinions of a bird, connected, like two choice animals, ye have sought our worship. Bright as the fire the votary hath kindled, ye sacrifice in many a spot as roamers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye are our kinsmen, like two sons, two fathers, strong in your splendour and like kings for conquest; Like rays for our enjoyment, Lords to feed us, ye, like quick bearers, have obeyed our calling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: You are like two pleasantly moving well-fed (hills) like Mitra and Varuna, the two bestowers of felicity, veracious, possessors of infinite wealth, happy, like two horses plump with fodder, abiding in the firmament, like two rams (are you) to be nourished with sacrificial food, to be cherished (with oblations).
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: You are like two mad elephants bending their forequarters and smiting the foe, like the two sons of Nitosa destroying (foes), and cherishing (friends); you are bright as two water-born (jewels), do you, who are victorious, (render) my decaying mortal body free from decay.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fierce (Asvins), like two powerful (heroes), you enable this moving, perishable mortal (frame) to cross over to the objects (of its destination) as over water; extremely strong, like the Rbhus, your chariot, attained its destination swift as the wind, it pervaded (everywhere), it dispensed riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With your bellies full of the Soma, like two saucepans, preservers of wealth, destroyers of enemies. (you are) armed with hatchets, moving like two flying (birds) with forms like the moon, attaining success through the mind, like two laudable beings, (you are) approaching (the sacrifice).
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like giants, ye will find firm ground to stand on in depths, like feet for one who fords a shallow. Like cars ye will attend to him who orders: ye Two enjoy our wondrous work as sharers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like toiling bees ye bring to us your honey, as bees into the hide that opens downward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we increase the laud and gain us vigour: come to our song, ye whom one chariot carries. Filled be our kine with ripened meath like glory: Bhutamsa hath fulfilled the Asvins' longing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THESE men's great bounty hath been manifested, and the whole world of life set free from darkness. Great light hath come, vouchsafed us by the Fathers: apparent is the spacious path of Guerdon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: High up in heaven abide the Guerdon-givers: they who give steeds dwell with the Sun for ever. They who give gold are blest with life eternal. they who give robes prolong their lives, O Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Not from the niggards-for they give not freely-comes Meed at sacrifice, Gods' satisfaction: Yea, many men with hands stretched out with Guerdon present their gifts because they dread dishonour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These who observe mankind regard oblation as streamy Vayu and light-finding Arka. They satisfy and give their gifts in synod, and pour in streams the seven-mothered Guerdon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who brings Guerdon comes as first invited: chief of the hamlet comes the Guerdon-bearer. Him I account the ruler of the people who was the first to introduce the Guerdon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They call him Rsi, Brahman, Sama-chanter, reciter of the laud, leader of worship. The brightly-shining God's three forms he knoweth who first bestowed the sacrificial Guerdon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Guerdon bestows the horse, bestows the bullock, Guerdon bestows, moreover, gold that Rsisters. Guerdon gives food which is our life and spirit. He who is wise takes Guerdon for his armour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The liberal die not, never are they ruined: the liberal suffer neither harm nor trouble. The light of heaven, the universe about us,-all this doth sacrificial Guerdon give them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: First have the liberal gained a fragrant dwelling, and got themselves a bride in fair apparel. The liberal have obtained their draught of liquor, and conquered those who, unprovoked, assailed them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They deck the fleet steed for the bounteous giver: the maid adorns herself and waits to meet him. His home is like a lake with lotus blossoms, like the Gods' palaces adorned and splendid.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Steeds good at draught convey the liberal giver, and lightly rolling moves the car of Guerdon. Assist, ye Gods, the liberal man in battles: the liberal giver conquers foes in combat.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHAT wish of Sarama hath brought her hither? The path leads far away to distant places. What charge hast thou for us? Where turns thy journey? How hast thou made thy way o'er Rasa's waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I come appointed messenger of Indra, seeking your ample stores of wealth, O Panis. This hath preserved me from the fear of crossing: thus have I made my way o'er Rasa's waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What is that Indra like, what is his aspect whose envoy, Sarama, from afar thou comest? Let him approach, and we will show him friendship: he shall be made the herdsman of our cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I know him safe from harm: but he can punish who sent me hither from afar as envoy. Him rivers flowing with deep waters bide not. Low will ye be, O Panis, slain by Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These are the kine which, Sarama, thou seekest, flying, O Blest One, to the ends of heaven. Who will loose these for thee without a battle? Yea, and sharp-pointed are our warlike weapons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even if your wicked bodies, O ye Panis, were arrow-proof, your words are weak for wounding; And were the path to you as yet unmastered, Brhaspati in neither case will spare you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Paved with the rock is this our treasure-chamber; filled full of precious things, of kine, and horses. These Panis who are watchful keepers guard it. In vain hast thou approached this lonely station.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rsis will come inspirited with Soma, Angirases unwearied, and Navagvas. This stall of cattle will they part among them: then will the Panis wish these words unspoken.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even thus, O Sarama, hast thou come hither, forced by celestial might to make the journey. Turn thee not back, for thou shalt be our sister: O Blest One, we will give thee of the cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Brotherhood, sisterhood, I know not either: the dread Angirases and Indra know them. They seemed to long for kine when I departed. Hence, into distance, be ye gone, O Panis.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hence, far away, ye Panis! Let the cattle lowing come forth as holy Law commandeth, Kine which Brhaspati, and Soma, Rsis, sages, and pressing-stones have found when hidden.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THESE first, the boundless Sea, and Matarisvan, fierce-glowing Fire, the Strong, the Bliss-bestower, And heavenly Floods, first-born by holy Order, exclaimed against the outrage on a Brahman.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: King Soma first of all, without reluctance, made restitution of the Brahman's consort. Mitra and Varuna were the inviters: Agni as Hota; took her hand and led her.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The man, her pledge, must by her hand be taken when they have cried, She is a Brahman's consort. She stayed not for a herald to conduct her: thus is the kingdom of a ruler guarded.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thus spake of her those Gods of old, Seven Rsis who sate them down to their austere devotion: Dire is a Brahman's wife led home by others: in the supremest heaven she plants confusion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Brahmacari goes engaged in duty: he is a member of the Gods' own body. Through him Brhaspati obtained his consort, as the Gods gained the ladle brought by Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So then the Gods restored her, so men gave the woman back again. The Kings who kept their promises restored the Brahman's wedded wife,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Having restored the Brahman's wife, and freed them, with Gods' aid, from sin, They shared the fulness of the earth, and won themselves extended sway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THOU in the house of man this day enkindled worshippest Gods as God, O Jatavedas. Observant, bright as Mitra, bring them hither: thou art a sapient and foreknowing envoy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Tanunapat, fair-tongued, with sweet meath balming the paths and ways of Order, make them pleasant. Convey our sacrifice to heaven, exalting with holy thoughts our hymns of praise and worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Invoked, deserving prayer and adoration, O Agni, come accordant with the Vasus. Thou art, O Youthful Lord, the Gods' Invoker, so, best of Sacrificers, bring them quickly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By rule the Sacred Grass is scattered eastward, a robe to clothe this earth when dawns are breaking. Widely it spreads around and far-extended, fair for the Gods and bringing peace and freedom.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let the expansive Doors be widely opened, like wives who deck their beauty for their husbands. Lofty, celestial, all-impelling Portals, admit the Gods and give them easy entrance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pouring sweet dews let holy Night and Morning, each close to each, he seated at their station, Lofty, celestial Dames with gold to deck them. assuming all their fair and radiant beauty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come the two first celestial sweet-voiced Hotars, arranging sacrifice for man to worship As singers who inspire us in assemblies, showing the eastward light with their direction.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let Bharati come quickly to our worship, and Ila showing like a human being. So let Sarasvati and both her fellows, deft Goddesses, on this fair grass be seated.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hotar more skilled in sacrifice, bring hither with speed to-day God Tvastar, thou who knowest. Even him who formed these two, the Earth and Heaven the Parents, with their forms, and every creature.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Send to our offerings which thyself thou balmest the Companies of Gods in ordered season. Agni, Vanaspati the Immolator sweeten our offered gift with meath and butter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, as soon as he was born, made ready the sacrifice, and was the Gods' preceder. May the Gods cat our offering consecrated according to this true Priest's voice and guidance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: BRING forth your sacred song ye prudent singers, even as are the thoughts of human beings. Let us draw Indra with true deeds anear us: he loves our songs, the Hero, and is potent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The hymn shone brightly from the seat of worship: to the kine came the Bull, the Heifer's Offspring With mighty bellowing hath he arisen, and hath pervaded even the spacious regions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra knows, verily, how to hear our singing, for he, victorious, made a path for Surya. He made the Cow, and be became the Sovran of Heaven, primeval, matchless, and unshaken.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praised by Angirases, Indra demolished with might the works of the great watery monster Full many regions, too, hath he pervaded, and by his truth supported earth's foundation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The counterpart of heaven and earth is Indra: he knoweth all libations, slayeth Susna. The vast sky with the Sun hath he extended, and, best otpillars, stayed it with a pillar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Vrtra-slaver with his bolt felled Vrtra: the magic of the godless, waxen mighty, Here hast thou, Bold Assailant, boldly conquered. Yea, then thine arms, O Maghavan, were potent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When the Dawns come attendant upon Surya their rays discover wealth of divers colours. The Star of heaven is seen as 'twere approaching: none knoweth aught of it as it departeth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Far have they gone, the first of all these waters, the waters that flowed forth when Indra sent them. Where is their spring, and where is their foundation? Where now, ye Waters, is your inmost centre?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou didst free rivers swallowed by the Dragon; and rapidly they set themselves in motion, Those that were loosed and those that longed for freedom. Excited now to speed they run unresting.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yearning together they have sped to Sindhu: the Fort-destroyer, praised, of old, hath loved them. Indra, may thy terrestrial treasures reach us, and our full songs of joy approach thy dwelling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: DRINK of the juice, O Indra, at thy plea. sure, for thy first draught is early morn's libation. Rejoice, that thou mayst slay our foes, O Hero, and we with lauds will tell thy mighty exploits.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou hast a car more swift than thought, O Indra; thereon come hither, come to drink the Soma. Let thy Bay Steeds, thy Stallions, hasten hither, with whom thou comest nigh and art delighted.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Deck out thy body with the fairest colours, with golden splendour of the Sun adorn it. O Indra, turn thee hitherward invited by us thy friends; be seated and be joyful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O thou whose grandeur in thy festive transports not even these two great worlds have comprehended. Come, Indra, with thy dear Bay Horses harnessed, come to our dwelling and the food thou lovest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pressed for thy joyous banquet is the Soma, Soma whereof thou, Indra, ever drinking, Hast waged unequalled battles with thy foemen, which prompts the mighty flow of thine abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Found from of old is this thy cup, O Indra: Satakratu, drink therefrom the Soma. Filled is the beaker with the meath that gladdens, the beaker which all Deities delight in.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From many a side with proffered entertainment the folk are calling thee, O Mighty Indra. These our libations shall for thee be richest in sweet meath: drink thereof and find them pleasant.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I will declare thy deeds of old, O Indra, the mighty acts which thou hast first accomplished. In genuine wrath thou loosenedst the mountain so that the Brahman easily found the cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lord of the hosts, amid our bands be seated: they call thee greatest Sage among the sages. Nothing is done, even far away, without thee: great, wondrous, Maghavan, is the hymn I sing thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Aim of our eyes be thou, for we implore thee, O Maghavan, Friend of friends and Lord of treasures. Fight, Warrior strong in truth, fight thou the battle: give us our share of undivided riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE Heavens and the Earth accordant with all Gods encouraged graciously that vigorous might of his. When he came showing forth his majesty and power, he drank of Soma juice and waxed exceeding strong.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This majesty of his Visnu extols and lauds, making the state that gives the meath flow forth with might. When Indra Maghavan with those who followed him had smitten Vrtra he deserved the choice of Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, bearing warlike weapons, fain to win thee praise, thou meetest Vrtra, yea, the Dragon, for the fight, Then all the Maruts who were gathered with dice there extolled, O Mighty One, thy powerful majesty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soon as he sprang to life he forced asunder hosts: forward the Hero looked to manly deed and war. He cleft the rock, he let concurrent streams flow forth, and with his skillful art stablished the heavens' wide vault.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra hath evermore possessed surpassing power: he forced, far from each other, heaven and earth apart. He hurled impetuous down his iron thunderbolt, a joy to Varuna's and Mitra's worshipper.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Then to the mighty powers of Indra, to his wrath, his the fierce Stormer, loud of voice, they came with speed; What time the Potent One rent Vrtra with his strength, who held the waters back, whom darkness compassed round.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even in the first of those heroic acts which they who strove together came with might to execute, Deep darkness fell upon the slain, and Indra won by victory the right of being first invoked.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Then all the Gods extolled, with eloquence inspired by draughts of Soma juice, thy deeds of manly might. As Agni eats the dry food with his tongue, he ate Vrtra, the Dragon, maimed by Indra's deadly dart.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Proclaim his many friendships, met with friendship, made with singers, with the skillful and the eloquent. Indra, when he subdues Dhuni and Cumuri, lists to Dabhiti for his faithful spirit's sake.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give riches manifold with noble horses, to be remembered while my songs address thee. May we by easy paths pass all our troubles: find us this day a ford wide and extensive.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Two perfect springs of heat pervade the Threefold, and come for their delight is Matarisvan. Craving the milk of heaven the Gods are present: well do they know the praisesong and the Saman.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The priests beard far away, as they are ordered, serve the three Nirrtis, for well they know them. Sages have traced the cause that first produced them, dwelling in distant and mysterious chambers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Youthful One, well-shaped, with four locks braided, brightened with oil, puts on the ordinances. Two Birds of mighty power are seated near her, there where the Deities receive their portion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: One of these Birds hath passed into the sea of air: thence he looks round and views this universal world. With simple heart I have beheld him from anear: his Mother kisses him and he returns her kiss.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him with fair wings though only One in nature, wise singers shape, with songs, in many figures. While they at sacrifices fix the metres, they measure out twelve chalices of Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: While they arrange the four and six-and-thirty, and duly order, up to twelve, the measures, Having disposed the sacrifice thoughtful sages send the Car forward with the Rc and Saman.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Chariot's majesties are fourteen others: seven sages lead it onward with their Voices. Who will declare to us the ford Apnana, the path whereby they drink first draughts of Soma?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The fifteen lauds are in a thousand places that is as vast as heaven and earth in measure. A thousand spots contain the mighty thousand. Vak spreadeth forth as far as Prayer extendeth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What sage hath learned the metres' application? Who hath gained Vak, the spirit's aim and object? Which ministering priest is called eighth Hero? Who then hath tracked the two Bay Steeds of Indra?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yoked to his chariot-pole there stood the Coursers: they only travel round earth's farthest limits. These, when their driver in his home is settled, receive the allotted meed of their exertion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: VERILY wondrous is the tender Youngling's growth who never draweth nigh to drink his Mothers' milk. As soon as she who hath no udder bore him, he, faring on his great errand, suddenly grew strong.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Then Agni was his name, most active to bestow, gathering up the trees with his consuming tooth; Skilled in fair sacrifice, armed with destroying tongue, impetuous as a bull that snorteth in the mead.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praise him, your God who, bird-like, rests upon a tree, scattering drops of juice and pouring forth his flood, Speaking aloud with flame as with his lips a priest, and broadening his paths like one of high command.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou Everlasting, whom, far-striding fain to burn, the winds, uninterrupted, never overcome, They have approached, as warriors eager for the fight, heroic Trita, guiding him to gain his wish.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This Agni is the best of Kanvas, Kanvas' Friend, Conqueror of the foe whether afar or near. May Agni guard the singers, guard the princes well: may Agni grant to us our princes' gracious help.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Do thou, Supitrya, swiftly following, make thyself the lord of Jatavedas, mightiest of all, Who surely gives a boon even in thirsty land most powerful, prepared to aid us in the wilds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thus noble Agni with princes and mortal men is lauded, excellent for conquering strength with chiefs, Men who are well-disposed as friends and true to Law, even as the heavens in majesty surpass mankind.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Son of Strength, Victorious, with this title Upastuta's most potent voice reveres thee. Blest with brave sons by thee we will extol thee, and lengthen out the days of our existence.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thus, Agni, have the sons of Vrstihavya, the Rsis, the Upastutas invoked thee. Protect them, guard the singers and the princes. With Vasat! have they come, with hands uplifted, with their uplifted hands and cries of Glory!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: DRINK Soma juice for mighty power and vigour, drink, Strongest One, that thou mayst smite down Vrtra. Drink thou, invoked, for strength, and riches: drink thou thy fill of meath and pour it down, O Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drink of the foodful juice stirred into motion, drink what thou choosest of the flowing Soma. Giver of weal, be joyful in thy spirit, and turn thee hitherward to bless and prosper.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let heavenly Soma gladden thee, O Indra, let that effused among mankind delight thee. Rejoice in that whereby thou gavest freedom, and that whereby thou conquerest thy foemen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let Indra come, impetuous, doubly mighty, to the poured juice, the Bull, with two Bay Coursers. With juices pressed in milk, with meath presented, glut evermore thy bolt, O Foe-destroyer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dash down, outflaming their sharp flaming weapons, the strong-holds of the men urged on by demons. I give thee, Mighty One, great strength and conquest: go, meet thy foes and rend them in the battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Extend afar the votary's fame and glory, as the firm archer's strength drives off the foeman. Ranged on our side, grown strong in might that conquers, never defeated, still increase thy body.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee have we presented this oblation: accept it, Sovran Ruler, free from anger. Juice, Maghavan, for thee is pressed and ripened: eat, Indra, drink of that which stirs to meet thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Eat, Indra, these oblations which approach thee: be pleased with food made ready and with Soma. With entertainment we receive thee friendly: effectual be the sacrificer's wishes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I send sweet speech to Indra and to Agni: with hymns I speed it like a boat through waters. Even thus, the Gods seem moving round about me, the fountains and bestowers of our riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE Gods have not ordained hunger to be our death: even to the well-fed man comes death in varied shape. The riches of the liberal never waste away, while he who will not give finds none to comfort him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The man with food in store who, when the needy comes in miserable case begging for bread to eat, Hardens his heart against him-even when of old he did him service-finds not one to comfort him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bounteous is he who gives unto the beggar who comes to him in want of food and feeble. Success attends him in the shout of battle. He makes a friend of him in future troubles.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: No friend is he who to his friend and comrade who comes imploring food, will offer nothing. Let him depart-no home is that to rest in-, and rather seek a stranger to support him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let the rich satisfy the poor implorer, and bend his eye upon a longer pathway. Riches come now to one, now to another, and like the wheels of cars are ever rolling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The foolish man wins food with fruitless labour: that food -I speak the truth- shall be his ruin. He feeds no trusty friend, no man to love him. All guilt is he who eats with no partaker.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The ploughshare ploughing makes the food that feeds us, and with its feet cuts through the path it follows. Better the speaking than the silent Brahman: the liberal friend out values him who gives not.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He with one foot hath far outrun the biped, and the two-footed catches the three-footed. Four-footed creatures come when bipeds call them, and stand and look where five are met together.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The hands are both alike: their labour differs. The yield of sister milch-kine is unequal. Twins even differ in their strength and vigour: two, even kinsmen, differ in their bounty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI, refulgent among men thou slayest the devouring fiend, Bright Ruler in thine own abode.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou springest up when worshipped well the drops of butter are thy joy When ladies are brought near to thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Honoured with gifts he shines afar, Agni adorable with song: The dripping ladle balms his face.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni with honey in his mouth, honoured with gifts, is balmed with oil, Refulgent in his wealth of light.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praised by our hymns thou kindlest thee, Oblation-bearer, for the Gods As such do mortals call on thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To that Immortal Agni pay worship with oil, ye mortal men,- Lord of the house, whom none deceives.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, burn the Raksasas with thine unconquerable flame Shine guardian of Eternal Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So, Agni, with thy glowing face burn fierce against the female fiends, Shining among Uruksayas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Uruksayas have kindled thee, Oblation-bearer, thee, with hymns. Best Worshipper among mankind.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THIS, even this was my resolve, to win a cow, to win a steed: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like violent gusts of wind the draughts that I have drunk have lifted me Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The draughts I drank have borne me up, as fleet-foot horses draw a car: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The hymn hath reached me, like a cow who lows to meet her darling calf: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As a wright bends a chariot-seat so round my heart I bend the hymn: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Not as a mote within the eye count the Five Tribes of men with me: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The heavens and earth themselves have not grown equal to one half of me Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I in my grandeur have surpassed the heavens and all this spacious earth Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Aha! this spacious earth will I deposit either here or there Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In one short moment will I smite the earth in fury here or there: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: One of my flanks is in the sky; I let the other trail below: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: 1, greatest of the Mighty Ones, am lifted to the firmament: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I seek the worshipper's abode; oblation-bearer to the Gods: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: IN all the worlds That was the Best and Highest whence sprang the Mighty Gods, of splendid valour. As soon as born he overcomes his foemen, be in whom all who lend him aid are joyful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Grown mighty in his strength, with ample vigour, he as a foe strikes fear into the Dasa, Eager to win the breathing and the breathless. All sang thy praise at banquet and oblation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All concentrate on thee their mental vigour, what time these, twice or thrice, are thine assistants. Blend what is sweeter than the sweet with sweetness: win. quickly with our meath that meath in battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Therefore in thee too, thou who winnest riches, at every banquet are the sages joyful. With mightier power, Bold God, extend thy firmness: let not malignant Yatudhanas harm thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Proudly we put our trust in thee in battles, when we behold great wealth the prize of combat. I with my words impel thy weapons onward, and sharpen with my prayer thy vital vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Worthy of praises, many-shaped, most skillful, most energetic, Aptya of the Aptyas: He with his might destroys the seven Danus, subduing many who were deemed his equals.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou in that house which thy protection guardeth bestowest wealth, the higher and the lower. Thou establishest the two much-wandering Mothers, and bringest many deeds to their completion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Brhaddiva, the foremost of light-winners, repeats these holy prayers, this strength of Indra. He rules the great self-luminous fold of cattle, and all the doors of light hath he thrown open.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thus hath Brhaddiva, the great Atharvan, spoken to Indra as himself in person. The spotless Sisters, they who are his Mothers, with power exalt him and impel him onward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: IN the beginning rose Hiranyagarbha, born Only Lord of all created beings. He fixed and holdeth up this earth and heaven. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Giver of vital breath, of power and vigour, he whose commandments all the Gods acknowledge -. The Lord of death, whose shade is life immortal. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who by his grandeur hath become Sole Ruler of all the moving world that breathes and slumbers; He who is Lord of men and Lord of cattle. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His, through his might, are these snow-covered mountains, and men call sea and Rasa his possession: His arms are these, his are these heavenly regions. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By him the heavens are strong and earth is steadfast, by him light's realm and sky-vault are supported: By him the regions in mid-air were measured. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him, supported by his help, two armies embattled look while trembling in their spirit, When over them the risen Sun is shining. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time the mighty waters came, containing the universal germ, producing Agni, Thence sprang the Gods' one spirit into being. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He in his might surveyed the floods containing productive force and generating Worship. He is the God of gods, and none beside him. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Neer may he harm us who is earth's Begetter, nor he whose laws are sure, the heavens' Creator, He who brought forth the great and lucid waters. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Prajapati! thou only comprehendest all these created things, and none beside thee. Grant us our hearts' desire when we invoke thee: may we have store of riches in possession.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I PRAISE the God of wondrous might like Indra, the lovely pleasant Guest whom all must welcome. May Agni, Priest and Master of the household, give hero strength and all-sustaining riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, graciously accept this song of mine, thou passing-wise who knowest every ordinance. Enwrapped in holy oil further the course of prayer: the Gods bestow according to thy holy law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Immortal, wandering round the seven stations, give, a liberal Giver, to the pious worshipper, Wealth, Agni, with brave sons and ready for his use: welcome the man who comes with fuel unto thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The seven who bring oblations worship thee, the Strong, the first, the Great Chief Priest, Ensign of sacrifice, The oil-anointed Bull, Agni who hears, who sends as God full hero strength to him who freely gives.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: First messenger art thou, meet for election: drink thou thy fill invited to the Anirta, The Maruts in the votary's house adorned thee; with lauds the Bhrgus gave thee light and glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Milking the teeming Cow for all-sustaining food. O Wise One, for the worship-loving worshipper, Thou, Agni, dropping oil, thrice lighting works of Law, showest thy wisdom circling home and sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who at flushing of this dawn appointed thee their messenger, these men have paid thee reverence. Gods strengthened thee for work that must be glorified, Agni, while they made butter pure for sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Arrangers in our synods, Agni, while they sang Vasisistha s sons have called thee down, the Potent One. Maintain the growth of wealth with men who sacrifice. Ye Gods, preserve us with your blessings evermore.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SEE, Vena, born in light, hath driven hither, on chariot of the air, the Calves of Prsni. Singers with hymns caress him as an infant there where the waters and the sunlight mingle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vena draws up his wave from out the ocean. mist-born, the fair one's back is made apparent, Brightly he shone aloft on Order's summit: the hosts sang glory to their common birthplace.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Full many, lowing to their joint-possession, dwelling together stood the Darling's Mothers. Ascending to the lofty height of Order, the bands of singers 'sip the sweets of Amrta.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Knowing his form, the sages yearned to meet him: they have come nigh to hear the wild Bull's bellow. Performing sacrifice they reached the river: for the Gandharva found the immortal waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Apsaras, the Lady, sweetly smiling, supports her Lover in sublimest heaven. In his Friend's dwelling as a Friend he wanders: he, Vena, rests him on his golden pinion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They gaze on thee with longing in their spirit, as on a strong-winged bird that mounteth sky-ward; On thee with wings of gold, Varuna's envoy, the Bird that hasteneth to the home of Yama.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Erect, to heaven hath the Gandharva mounted, pointing at us his many-coloured weapons; Clad in sweet raiment beautiful to look on, for he, as light, produceth forms that please us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When as a spark he cometh near the ocean, still looking with a vulture's eye to heaven, His lustre, joying in its own bright splendour, maketh dear glories in the lowest region.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: COME to this sacrifice of ours, O Agni, threefold, with seven threads and five divisions. Be our oblation-bearer and preceder: thou hast lain long enough in during darkness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I come a God foreseeing from the godless to immortality by secret pathways, While I, ungracious one, desert the gracious, leave mine own friends and seek the kin of strangers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I, looking to the guest of other lineage, have founded many a rule of Law and Order. I bid farewell to the Great God, the Father, and, for neglect, obtain my share of worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I tarried many a year within this altar: I leave the Father, for my choice is Indra. Away pass Agni, Varuna and Soma. Rule ever changes: this I come to favour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These Asuras have lost their powers of magic. But thou, O Varuna, if thou dost love me, O King, discerning truth and right from falsehood, come and be Lord and Ruler of my kingdom.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here is the light of heaven, here all is lovely; here there is radiance, here is air's wide region. Let us two slaughter Vrtra. Forth, O Soma! Thou art oblation: we therewith will serve thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Sage hath fixed his form by wisdom in the heavens: Varuna with no violence let the waters flow. Like women-folk, the floods that bring prosperity have you lit his hue and colour as they gleamed and shone.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These wait upon his loftiest power and vigour: he dwells in these who triumph in their Godhead; And they, like people who elect their ruler, have in abhorrence turned away from Vrtra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They call him Swan, the abhorrent floods' Companion, moving in friendship with celestial Waters. The poets in their thought have looked on Indra swiftly approaching when Anustup calls him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I TRAVEL with the Rudras and the Vasus, with the Adityas and All-Gods I wander. I hold aloft both Varuna and Mitra, Indra and Agni, and the Pair of Asvins.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I cherish and sustain high-swelling Soma, and Tvastar I support, Pusan, and Bhaga. I load with wealth the zealous sacrificer who pours the juice and offers his oblation
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I am the Queen, the gatherer-up of treasures, most thoughtful, first of those who merit worship. Thus Gods have stablished me in many places with many homes to enter and abide in.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Through me alone all eat the food that feeds them,-each man who sees, breathes, hears the word outspoken They know it not, but yet they dwell beside me. Hear, one and all, the truth as I declare it.
