verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I, verily, myself announce and utter the word that Gods and men alike shall welcome. I make the man I love exceeding mighty, make him a sage, a Rsi, and a Brahman.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I bend the bow for Rudra that his arrow may strike and slay the hater of devotion. I rouse and order battle for the people, and I have penetrated Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: On the world's summit I bring forth the Father: my home is in the waters, in the ocean. Thence I extend o'er all existing creatures, and touch even yonder heaven with my forehead.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I breathe a strong breath like the wind and tempest, the while I hold together all existence. Beyond this wide earth and beyond the heavens I have become so mighty in my grandeur.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: No peril, no severe distress, ye Gods, affects the mortal man, Whom Aryaman and Mitra lead, and Varima, of one accord, beyond his foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This very thing do we desire, Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman, Whereby ye guard the mortal man from sore distress, and lead him safe beyond his foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These are, each one, our present helps, Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman. Best leaders, best deliverers to lead us on and bear as safe beyond our foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye compass round and guard each man, Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman: In your dear keeping may we be, ye who are excellent as guides beyond our foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Adityas are beyond all foes,-Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman: Strong Rudra with the Marut host, Indra, Agni let us call for weal beyond our foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These lead us safely over all, Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman, These who are Kings of living men, over all troubles far away beyond our foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May they give bliss to aid us well, Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman: May the Adityas, when we pray, grant us wide shelter and defense beyond our foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As in this place, O Holy Ones, ye Vasus freed even the Gaud when her feet were fettered. So free us now from trouble and affliction: and let our life be lengthened still, O Api.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WITH all her eyes the Goddess Night looks forth approaching many a spot: She hath put all her glories on.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Immortal. she hath filled the waste, the Goddess hath filled height and depth: She conquers darkness with her light.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Goddess as she comes hath set the Dawn her Sister in her place: And then the darkness vanishes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So favour us this night, O thou whose pathways we have visited As birds their nest upon the tree.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The villagers have sought their homes, and all that walks and all that flies, Even the falcons fain for prey.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Keep off the she-wolf and the wolf, O Urmya, keep the thief away; Easy be thou for us to pass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Clearly hath she come nigh to me who decks the dark with richest hues: O Morning, cancel it like debts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These have I brought to thee like kine. O Night, thou Child of Heaven, accept This laud as for a conqueror.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LET me win glory, Agni, in our battles: enkindling thee, may we support our bodies. May the four regions bend and bow before me: with thee for guardian may we win in combat.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May all the Gods be on my side in battle, the Maruts led by Indra, Visnu, Agni. Mine be the middle air's extended region, and may the wind blow favouring these my wishes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the Gods grant me riches; may the blessing and invocation of the Gods assist me. Foremost in fight be the divine Invokers: may we, unwounded, have brave heroes round us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For me let them present all mine oblations, and let my mind's intention be accomplished. May I he guiltless of the least transgression: and, all ye Go-is, do ye combine to bless us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye six divine Expanses, grant us freedom: here, all ye Gods, acquit yourselves like heroes. Let us not lose our children or our bodies: let us not benefit the foe, King Soma!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Baffling the wrath of our opponents, Agni, guard us as our infallible Protector. Let these thy foes turn back and seek their houses, and let their thought who watch at home be ruined.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lord of the world, Creator of creators the saviour God who overcomes the foeman. May Gods, Brhaspati, both Asvins shelter from ill this sacrifice and sacrificer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Foodful, and much-invoked, at this our calling may the great Bull vouchsafe us wide protection. Lord of Bay Coursers, Indra, blew our children: harm us not, give us riot as prey to others.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let those who are our foemen stay. afar from us: with Indra and with Agni we will drive them off. Vasus, Adityas, Rudras have exalted me, made me far-reaching, mighty, thinker, sovran lord.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THEN was not non-existent nor existent: there was no realm of air, no sky beyond it. What covered in, and where? and what gave shelter? Was water there, unfathomed depth of water?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Death was not then, nor was there aught immortal: no sign was there, the day's and night's divider. That One Thing, breathless, breathed by its own nature: apart from it was nothing whatsoever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Darkness there was: at first concealed in darkness this All was indiscriminate chaos. All that existed then was void and formless: by the great power of Warmth was born that Unit.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thereafter rose Desire in the beginning, Desire, the primal seed and germ of Spirit. Sages who searched with their heart's thought discovered the existent's kinship in the non-existent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Transversely was their severing line extended: what was above it then, and what below it? There were begetters, there were mighty forces, free action here and energy up yonder
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who verily knows and who can here declare it, whence it was born and whence comes this creation? The Gods are later than this world's production. Who knows then whence it first came into being?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, the first origin of this creation, whether he formed it all or did not form it, Whose eye controls this world in highest heaven, he verily knows it, or perhaps he knows not.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE sacrifice drawn out with threads on every side, stretched by a hundred sacred ministers and one,- This do these Fathers weave who hitherward are come: they sit beside the warp and cry, Weave forth, weave back.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Man extends it and the Man unbinds it: even to this vault of heaven hath he outspun, it. These pegs are fastened to the seat of worship: they made the Sama-hymns their weaving shuttles.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What were the rule, the order and the model? What were the wooden fender and the butter? What were the hymn, the chant, the recitation, when to the God all Deities paid worship?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Closely was Gayatri conjoined with Agni, and closely Savitar combined with Usnih. Brilliant with Ukthas, Soma joined Anustup: Brhaspati's voice by Brhati was aided.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Viraj adhered to Varuna and Mitra: here Tristup day by day was Indra's portion. Jagati entered all the Gods together: so by this knowledge men were raised to Rsis.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So by this knowledge men were raised to Rsis, when ancient sacrifice sprang up, our Fathers. With the mind's eye I think that I behold them who first performed this sacrificial worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who were versed in ritual and metre, in hymns and rules, were the Seven Godlike Rsis. Viewing the path of those of old, the sages have taken up the reins like chariot-drivers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: DRIVE all our enemies away, O Indra, the western, mighty Conqueror, and the eastern. Hero, drive off our northern foes and southern, that we in thy wide shelter may be joyful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What then? As men whose fields are full of barley reap the ripe corn removing it in order, So bring the food of those men, bring it hither, who went not to prepare the grass for worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Men come not with one horse at sacred seasons; thus they obtain no honour in assemblies. Sages desiring herds of kine and horses strengthen the mighty Indra for his friendship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye, Asvins, Lords of Splendour, drank full draughts of grateful Soma juice, And aided Indra in his work with Namuci of Asura birth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As parents aid a son, both Asvins, Indra, aided thee with their wondrous Powers and wisdom. When thou, with might. hadst drunk the draught that gladdens, Sarasvati, O Maghavan, refreshed thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra is strong to save, rich in assistance may he, possessing all, be kind and gracious. May he disperse our foes and give us safety, and may we be the lords of hero vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we enjoy his favour, his the Holy may we enjoy his blessed loving kindness. May this rich Indra, as our good Protector, drive off and keep afar all those who hate us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MAY Dyaus the Lord of lauded wealth, and Earth stand by the man who offers sacrifice, And may the Asvins, both the Gods, strengthen the worshipper with bliss.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As such we honour you, Mitra and Varuna, with hasty zeal, most blest, you who sustain the folk. So may we, through your friendship for the worshipper, subdue the fiends.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And when we seek to win your love and friendship, we who have precious wealth in our possession, Or when the worshipper augments his riches let not his treasures be shut up
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That other, Asura! too was born of Heaven. thou art, O Varuna, the King of all men. The chariot's Lord was well content, forbearing to anger Death by sin so great. This sin hath Sakaputa here committed. Heroes who fled to their dear friend he slayeth, When the Steed bringeth down your grace and favour in bodies dear and worshipful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Your Mother Aditi, ye wise, was purified with water even as earth is purified from heaven. Show love and kindness here below: wash her in rays of heavenly light.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye Twain have seated you as Lords of Wealth, as one who mounts a car to him who sits upon the pole, upon the wood. These our disheartened tribes Nrmedhas saved from woe, Sumedhas saved from Woe.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SING strength to Indra that shall set his chariot in the foremost place. Giver of room in closest fight, slayer of foes in shock of war, be thou our great encourager. Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of feeble enemies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou didst destroy the Dragon: thou sentest the rivers down to earth. Foeless, O Indra, wast thou born. Thou tendest well each choicest thing. Therefore we draw us close to thee. Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of feeble enemies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Destroyed be all malignities and all our enemy's designs. Thy bolt thou castest, at the foe, O Indra, who would smite us dead: thy liberal bounty gives us wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The robber people round about, Indra, who watch and aim at us,- Trample them down beneath thy foot; a conquering scatterer art thou.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoso assails us, Indra, be the man a stranger or akin, Bring down, thyself, his strength although it be as vast as are the heavens.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Close to thy friendship do we cling, O Indra, and depend, or, thee. Lead us beyond all pain and grief along the path of holy Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Do thou bestow upon us her, O Indra, who yields according to the singer's longing, That the great Cow may, with exhaustless udder, pouring a thousand streams, give milk to feed us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As, like the Morning, thou hast filled, O Indra, both the earth and heaven. So as the Mighty One, great King of all the mighty world of men, the Goddess Mother brought thee forth, the Blessed Mother gave thee life.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Relax that mortal's stubborn strength whose heart is bent on wickedness. Trample him down beneath thy feet who watches for and aims at us. The Goddess Mother brought thee forth, the Blessed Mother gave thee life.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Shake down, O Slayer of the foe, those great all splendid enemies. With all thy powers, O Sakra, all thine helps, O Indra, shake them down:
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As thou, O Satakratu, thou, O Indrv, shakest all things down As wealth for him who sheds the juice, with thine assistance thousandfold.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Around, on every side like drops of sweat let lightning-flashes fall. Let all malevolence pass away from us like threads of Darva grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou bearest in thine hand a lance like a long hook, great Counsellor! As with his foremost foot a goat, draw down the branch, O Maghavan.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Never, O Gods, do we offend, nor are we ever obstinate: we walk as holy texts command. Closely we clasp and cling to you, cling to your sides, beneath your arms.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: IN the Tree clothed with goodly leaves where Yama drinketh with the Gods, The Father, Master of the house, tendeth with love our ancient Sires.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I looked reluctantly on him who cherishes those men of old, On him who treads that evil path, and then I yearned for this again.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou mountest, though thou dost not see, O Child, the new and wheel-less car Which thou hast fashioned mentally, one poled but turning every way.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The car which thou hast made to roll hitherward from the Sages, Child! This hath the Saman followed close, hence, laid together on a ship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who was the father of the child? Who made the chariot roll away? Who will this day declare to us how the funeral gift was made?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When the funeral gift was placed, straightway the point of flame appeared. A depth extended in the front: a passage out was made behind.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here is the seat where Yama dwells, that which is called the Home of Gods: Here minstrels blow the flute for him here he is glorified with songs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HE with the long loose locks supports Agni, and moisture, heaven, and earth: He is all sky to look upon: he with long hair is called this light.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Munis, girdled with the wind, wear garments soiled of yellow hue. They, following the wind's swift course go where the Gods have gone before.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Transported with our Munihood we have pressed on into the winds: You therefore, mortal men. behold our natural bodies and no more.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Muni, made associate in the holy work of every God, Looking upon all varied forms flies through the region of the air.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Steed of Vata, Vayu's friend, the Muni, by the Gods impelled, In both the oceans hath his home, in eastern and in western sea.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Treading the path of sylvan beasts, Gandharvas, and Apsarases, He with long locks, who knows the wish, is a sweet most delightful friend
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vayu hath churned for him: for him he poundeth things most hard to bend, When he with long loose locks hath drunk, with Rudra, water from the cup.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: YE Gods, raise up once more the man whom ye have humbled and brought low. O Gods, restore to life again the man who hath committed sin.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Two several winds are blowing here, from Sindhu, from a distant land. May one breathe energy to thee, the other blow disease away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hither, O Wind, blow healing balm, blow all disease away, thou Wind; For thou who hast all medicine comest as envoy of the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I am come nigh to thee with balms to give thee rest and keep thee safe. I bring thee blessed strength, I drive thy weakening malady away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here let the Gods deliver him, the Maruts' band deliver him: All things that be deliver him that he be freed from his disease.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Waters have their healing power, the Waters drive disease away. The Waters have a balm for all: let them make medicine for thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The tongue that leads the voice precedes. Then with our ten-fold branching hands, With these two chasers of disease we stroke thee with a gentle touch.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: ALLIED with thee in friendship, Indra, these, thy priests, remembering Holy Law, rent Vrtra limb from limb, When they bestowed the Dawns and let the waters flow, and when thou didst chastise dragons at Kutsa's call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou sentest forth productive powers, clavest the hills, thou dravest forth the kine, thou drankest pleasant meath. Thou gavest increase through this Tree's surpassing might. The Sun shone by the hymn that sprang from Holy Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In the mid-way of heaven the Sun unyoked his car: the Arya found a match to meet his Dam foe. Associate with Rjisvan Indra overthrew the solid forts of Pipru, conjuring Asura.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He boldly cast down forts which none had e'er assailed: unwearied he destroyed the godless treasure-stores. Like Sun and Moon he took the stronghold's wealth away, and, praised in song, demolished foes with flashing dart.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Armed with resistless weapons, with vast power to cleave, the Vrtra-slayer whets his darts and deals fordi wounds. Bright Usas was afraid of Indra's slaughtering bolt: she went upon her way and left her chariot there.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These are thy famous exploits, only thine, when thou alone hast left the other bereft of sacrifice. Thou in the heavens hast set the ordering of the Moons: the Father bears the felly portioned out by thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SAVITAR, golden-haired, hath lifted eastward, bright With the sunbeams, his eternal lustre; He in whose energy wise Pusan marches, surveying all existence like a herdsman.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Beholding men he sits amid the heaven filling the two world-halves and air's wide region. He looks upon the rich far-spreading pastures between the eastern and the western limit.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, root of wealth, the gatherer-up of treasures, looks with his might on every form and figure. Savitar, like a God whose Law is constant, stands in the battle for the spoil like Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Waters from sacrifice came to the Gandharva Visvavasu, O Soma, when they saw him. Indra, approaching quickly, marked their going, and looked around upon the Sun's enclosures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This song Visvavasu shall sing us, meter of air's mid-realm celestial Gandharva, That we may know aright both truth and falsehood: may he inspire our thoughts and help our praises.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In the floods' track he found the booty seeker: the rocky cow-pen's doors he threw wide open. These, the Gandharva told him, Rowed with Amrta. Indra knew well the puissance of the dragons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI, life-power and fame are thine: thy fires blaze mightily, thou rich in wealth of beams! Sage, passing bright, thou givest to the worshipper, with strength, the food that merits laud.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With brilliant, purifying sheen, with perfect sheen thou liftest up thyself in light. Thou, visiting both thy Mothers, aidest them as Son: thou joinest close the earth and heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Jatavedas, Son of Strength, rejoice thyself, gracious, in our fair hymns and songs. In thee are treasured various forms of strengthening food, born nobly and of wondrous help.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, spread forth, as Ruler, over living things: give wealth to us, Immortal God. Thou shinest out from beauty fair to look upon: thou leadest us to conquering power.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him, the wise, who orders sacrifice, who hath great riches un der his control, Thou givest blest award of good, and plenteous food, givest him wealth that conquers all.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The men have set before them them for their welfare Agni, strong, visible to all, the Holy. Thee, Godlike One, with ears to hear, most famous, men's generations magnify with praise-songs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: TURN hither, Agni, speak to us: come to us with a gracious mind. Enrich us, Master of the house: thou art the Giver of our wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let Aryaman vouchsafe us wealth, and Bhaga, and Brhaspati. Let the Gods give their gifts, and let Sunrta, Goddess, grant us wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We call King Soma to our aid, and Agni with our songs and hymns, Adityas, Visnu, Surya, and the Brahman Priest Brhaspati.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, Vayu, Brhaspati, Gods swift to listen, we invoke, That in the synod all the folk may be benevolent to us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Urge Aryaman to send us gifts, and Indra, and Brhaspati, Vata, Visnu, Sarasvati and the Strong Courser Savitar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Do thou, O Agni, with thy fires strengthen our prayer and sacrifice: Urge givers to bestow their wealth to aid our service of the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WITH thee, O Agni, was this singer of the laud: he hath no other kinship, O thou Son of Strength. Thou givest blessed shelter with a triple guard. Keep the destructive lightning far away from us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy birth who seekest food is in the falling flood, Agni: as Comrade thou winnest all living things. Our coursers and our songs shall be victorious: they of themselves advance like one who guards the herd.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And thou, O Agni, thou of Godlike nature, sparest the stones, while caring up the brushwood. Then are thy tracks like deserts in the corn-lands. Let us not stir to wrath thy mighty arrow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O'er hills through vales devouring as thou goest, thou partest like an army fain for booty As when a barber shaves a beard, thou shavest earth when the wind blows on thy flame and fans it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Apparent are his lines as he approaches the course is single, but the cars are many, When, Agni, thou, making thine arms resplendent, advancest o'er the land spread out beneath thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now let thy strength, thy burning flames fly upward, thine energies, O Agni, as thou toilest. Gape widely, bend thee, waxing in thy vigour: let all the Vasus sit this day beside thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is the waters' reservoir, the great abode of gathered streams. Take thou another path than this, and as thou listest walk thereon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: On thy way hitherward and hence let flowery Durva grass spring up Let there be lakes with lotus blooms. These are the mansions of the flood.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: YE made that Atri, worn with eld, free as a horse to win the goal. When ye restored to youth and strength Kaksivan like a car renewed,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye freed that Atri like a horse, and brought him newly-born to earth. Ye loosed him like a firm-tied knot which Gods unsoiled by dust had bound.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Heroes who showed most wondrous power to Atri, strive to win fair songs; For then, O Heroes of the sky, your hymn of praise shall cease no more.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This claims your notice, Bounteous Gods! - oblation, Asvins! and our love, That ye, O Heroes, in the fight may bring us safe to ample room.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye Twain to Bhujyu tossed about in ocean at the region's end, Nasatyas, with your winged steeds came nigh, and gave him strength to win.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come with your joys, most liberal Gods, Lords of all treasures, bringing weal. Like fresh full waters to a well, so, Heroes come and be with us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THIS deathless Indu, like a steed, strong and of full vitality, Belongs to thee, the Orderer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here, by us, for the worshipper, is the wise bolt that works with skill. It brings the bubbling beverage as a dexterous man brings the effectual strong drink.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Impetuous Ahisuva, a bull among cows of his, looked down upon the restless Hawk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That the strong-pinioned Bird hath brought, Child of the Falcon, from afar, What moves upon a hundred wheels along the female Dragon's path.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Which, fair, unrobbed, the Falcon brought thee in his foot, the red-hued dwelling of the juice; Through this came vital power which lengthens out our days, and kinship through its help awoke.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So Indra is by lndu's power; e'en among Gods will it repel great treachery. Wisdom, Most Sapient One, brings force that lengthens life. May wisdom bring the juice to us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FROM out the earth I dig this plant, a herb of most effectual power, Wherewith one quells the rival wife and gains the husband for oneself.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Auspicious, with expanded leaves, sent by the Gods, victorious plant, Blow thou the rival wife away, and make my husband only mine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Stronger am 1, O Stronger One, yea, mightier than the mightier; And she who is my rival wife is lower than the lowest dames.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Her very name I utter not: she takes no pleasure in this man. Far into distance most remote drive we the rival wife away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I am the conqueror, and thou, thou also act victorious: As victory attends us both we will subdue my fellow-wife.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I have gained thee for vanquisher, have grasped thee with a stronger spell. As a cow hastens to her calf, so let thy spirit speed to me, hasten like water on its way.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GODDESS of wild and forest who seemest to vanish from the sight. How is it that thou seekest not the village? Art thou not afraid?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time the grasshopper replies and swells the shrill cicada's voice, Seeming to sound with tinkling bells, the Lady of the Wood exults.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And, yonder, cattle seem to graze, what seems a dwelling-place appears: Or else at eve the Lady of the Forest seems to free the wains.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here one is calling to his cow, another there hath felled a tree: At eve the dweller in the wood fancies that somebody hath screamed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Goddess never slays, unless some murderous enemy approach. Man eats of savoury fruit and then takes, even as he wills, his rest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now have I praised the Forest Queen, sweet-scented, redolent of balm, The Mother of all sylvan things, who tills not but hath stores of food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I TRUST in thy first wrathful deed, O Indra, when thou slewest Vrtra and didst work to profit man; What time the two world-halves fell short of thee in might, and the earth trembled at thy force, O Thunder-anned.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou with thy magic powers didst rend the conjurer Vrtra, O Blameless One, with heart that longed for fame. Heroes elect thee when they battle for the prey, thee in all sacrifices worthy of renown.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: God Much-invoked, take pleasure in these princes here, who, thine exalters, Maghavan, have come to wealth. In synods, when the rite succeeds, they hymn the Strong for sons and progeny and riches undisturbed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That man shall find delight in well-protected wealth whose care provides for him the quick-sought joyous draught. Bringing oblations, strengthened Maghavan, by thee, he swiftly wins the spoil with heroes in the fight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now for our band, O Maghavan, when lauded, make ample room with might, and grant us riches. Magician thou, our Varuna and Mitra, deal food to us, O Wondrous, as Dispenser.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHEN we have pressed the juice we laud thee, Indra, and when, Most Valorous we have won the booty. Bring us prosperity, as each desires it under thine own protection may we conquer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sublime from birth, mayst thou O Indra, Hero, with Surya overcome the Dasa races. As by a fountain's side, we bring the Soma that lay concealed, close-hidden in the waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Answer the votary's hymns, for these thou knowest, craving the Rsis' prayer, thyself a Singer May we be they who take delight in Somas: these with sweet food for thee, O Chariot-rider.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These holy prayers, O Indra, have I sung thee: grant to the men the strength of men, thou Hero. Be of one mind with those in whom thou joyest: keep thou the singers safe and their companions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Listen to Prthi's call, heroic Indra, and be thou lauded by the hymns of Venya, Him who hath sung thee to thine oil-rich dwelling, whose rolling songs have sped thee like a torrent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SAVITAR fixed the earth with bands to bind it, and made heaven steadfast where no prop supported. Savitar milked, as 'twere a restless courser, air, sea bound fast to what no foot had trodden.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Well knoweth Savitar, O Child of Waters, where ocean, firmly fixt, o'erflowed its limit. Thence sprang the world, from that uprose the region: thence heaven spread out and the wide earth expanded.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Then, with a full crowd of Immortal Beings, this other realm came later, high and holy. First, verily, Savitar's strong-pinioned Eagle was born: and he obeys his law for ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As warriors to their steeds, kine to their village, as fond milk giving cows approach their youngling, As man to wife, let Savitar come downward to us, heaven's bearer, Lord of every blessing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like the Angirasa Hiranvastupa, I call thee, Savitar, to this achievement: So worshipping and lauding thee for favour I watch for thee as for the stalk of Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THOU, bearer of oblations, though kindled, art kindled for the Gods. With the Adityas, Rudras, Vasus, come to us: to show us favour come to us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come hither and accept with joy this sacrifice and hymn of ours. O kindled God, we mortals are invoking thee, calling on thee to show us grace.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I laud thee Jatavedas, thee Lord of all blessings, with my song. Agni, bring hitherward the Gods whose Laws we love, whose laws we love, to show us grace.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni the God was made the great High-Priest of Gods, Rsis have kindled Agni, men of mortal mould. Agni I invocate for winning ample wealth. kindly disposed for winning wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Atri and Bharadvaja and Gavisthira, Kanva and Trasadasyu, in our fight he helped. On Agni calls Vasistha, even the household priest, the household priest to win his grace.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By Faith is Agni kindled, through Faith is oblation offered up. We celebrate with praises Faith upon the height of happiness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bless thou the man who gives, O Faith; Faith, bless the man who fain would give. Bless thou the liberal worshippers: bless thou the word that I have said.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even as the Deities maintained Faith in the mighty Asuras, So make this uttered wish of mine true for the liberal worshippers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Guarded by Vayu, Gods and men who sacrifice draw near to Faith. Man winneth Faith by yearnings of the heart, and opulence by Faith.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Faith in the early morning, Faith at noonday will we invocate, Faith at the setting of the Sun. O Faith, endow us with belief.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A MIGHTY Governor art thou, Wondrous, Destroyer of the foe, Whose friend is never done to death, and never, never overcome.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lord of the clan, who brings us bliss, Strong, Warrior, Slayer of the fiend, May India, Soma-drinker, go before us, Bull who gives us peace.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drive Raksasas and foes away, break thou in pieces Vrtra's jaws: O Vrtra-slaying Indra, quell the foeman's wrath who threatens us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra, beat our foes away, humble the men who challenge us: Send down to nether darkness him who seeks to do us injury.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Baffle the foeman's plan, ward off his weapon who would conquer us. Give shelter from his furious wrath, and keep his murdering dart afar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SWAYING about, the Active Ones came nigh to Indra at his birth, And shared his great heroic might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Based upon strength and victory and power, O Indra is thy birth: Thou, Mighty One, art strong indeed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou art the Vrtra-slayer, thou, Indra, hast spread the firmament: Thou hast with might upheld the heavens.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Indra, bearest in thine arms the lightning that accords with thee, Whetting thy thunderbolt with might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Indra, art preeminent over all creatures in thy might: Thou hast pervaded every place.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FOR some is Soma purified, some sit by sacrificial oil: To those for whom the meath flows forth, even to those let him depart.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Invincible through Fervour, those whom Fervour hath advanced to heaven, Who showed great Fervour in their lives, even to those let him depart.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The heroes who contend in war and boldly cast their lives away, Or who give guerdon thousandfold, even to those let him depart.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, the first followers of Law, Law's pure and holy strengtheners, The Fathers, Yama! Fervour-moved, even to those let him depart.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Skilled in a thousand ways and means, the sages who protect the Sun, The Rsis, Yama! Fervour-moved, even to those let him depart.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: ARAYI, one-eyed limping hag, fly, ever-screeching, to the hill. We frighten thee away with these, the heroes of Sirimbitha.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Scared from this place and that is she, destroyer of each germ unborn. Go, sharp-horned Brahmanaspti and drive Arayi far away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yon log that floats without a man to guide it on the river's edge,- Seize it, thou thing with hideous jaws, and go thou far away thereon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, foul with secret stain and spot, ye hastened onward to the breast, All Indra's enemies were slain and passed away like froth and foam.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These men have led about the cow, have duly carried Agni round, And raised their glory to the Gods. Who will attack them with success?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LET songs of ours speed Agni forth like a fleet courser in the race, And we will win each prize through him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni the dart whereby we gain kine for ourselves with help from thee,- That send us for the gain of wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, bring us wealth secure, vast wealth in horses and in kine: Oil thou the socket, turn the wheel.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, thou hast made the Sun, Eternal Star, to mount the sky, Bestowing light on living men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Agni, art the people's light, best, dearest, seated in thy shrine: Watch for the singer, give him life.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WE will, with Indra and all Gods to aid us, bring these existing worlds into subjection.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Our sacrifice, our bodies, and our offspring, let Indra form together with Adityas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With the Adityas, with the band of Maruts, may Indra be Protector of our bodies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As when the Gods came, after they had slaughtered the Asuras, keeping safe their Godlike nature,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Brought the Sun hitherward with mighty powers, and looked about them on their vigorous Godhead.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MAY Surya guard us out of heaven, and Vata from the firmament, And Agni from terrestrial spots.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou Savitar whose flame deserves hundred libations, be thou pleased: From failing lightning keep us safe.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Savitar the God, and may Parvata also give us sight; May the Creator give us sight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give sight unto our eye, give thou our bodies sight that they may see: May we survey, discern this world.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thus, Surya, may we look on thee, on thee most lovely to behold, See clearly with the eyes of men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: YON Sun hath mounted up, and this my happy fate hate mounted high. I knowing this, as conqueror have won my husband for mine own.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I am the banner and the head, a mighty arbitress am I: I am victorious, and my Lord shall be submissive to my will.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: My Sons are slayers of the foe, my Daughter is a ruling Queen: I am victorious: o'er my Lord my song of triumph is supreme.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Oblation, that which Indra gave and thus grew glorious and most high,- This have I offered, O ye Gods, and rid me of each rival wife.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Destroyer of the rival wife, Sole Spouse, victorious, conqueror, The others' glory have I seized as 'twere the wealth of weaker Dames.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I have subdued as conqueror these rivals, these my fellow-wives, That I may hold imperial sway over this Hero and the folk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: TASTE this strong draught enriched with offered viands: with all thy chariot here unyoke thy Coursers. Let not those other sacrificers stay thee, Indra: these juices shed for thee are ready.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thine is the juice effused, thine are the juices yet to be pressed: our resonant songs invite thee. O Indra, pleased to-day with this libation, come, thou who knowest all and drink the Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoso, devoted to the God, effuses Soma for him with yearning heart and spirit,- Never doth Indra give away his cattle: for him he makes the lovely Soma famous.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He looks with loving favour on the mortal who, like a rich man, pours for him the Soma. Maghavan in his bended arm supports him: he slays, unasked, the men who hate devotion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We call on thee to come to us, desirous of goods and spoil, of cattle, and of horses. For thy new love and favour are we present: let us invoke thee, Indra, as our welfare.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FOR life I set thee free by this oblation from the unknown decline and from Consumption; Or, if the grasping demon have possessed him, free him from her, O Indra, thou and Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be his days ended, be he now departed, be he brought very near to death already, Out of Destruction's lap again I bring him, save him for life to last a hundred autumns.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With hundred-eyed oblation, hundred-autumned, bringing a hundred lives, have I restored him, That Indra for a hundred years may lead him safe to the farther shore of all misfortune.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Live, waxing in thy strength, a hundred autumns, live through a hundred springs, a hundred winters. Through hundred-lived oblation Indra, Agni, Brhaspati, Savitar yield him for a hundred!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So have I found and rescued thee thou hast returned with youth renewed. Whole in thy members! I have found thy sight and all thy life for thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary
